structured.condensed: Stores base data about any business entity (sole-proprietor, corporation, society, etc.) that can interact with people and other businesses. Entry point: the Business class is instantiated by external code; this chunk shows no permission check. Core data: identifier (validated via Business.validate_identifier), legal_name, legal_type, state (ACTIVE, HISTORICAL, LIQUIDATION), tax_id, founding_date, dissolution_date. Decision: on identifier setter, if Business.validate_identifier(value) returns false, raises BusinessException('invalid-identifier-format', 406); otherwise sets _identifier. Stores derived classifications: legal_type mapped to LegalTypes enum (41 types including COOP, COMP, BCOMP, FOREIGN, SOCIETY, SOLE_PROP, PARTNERSHIP, etc.); CORPS list groups 8 incorporation types; LIMITED_COMPANIES and UNLIMITED_COMPANIES group by liability; AssociationTypes handles cooperatives and sole-proprietorships; BUSINESSES dict maps 4 incorporation types to numbered legal name suffixes and descriptions. Tracks filing history: last_ar_date, last_agm_date, last_coa_date, last_cod_date, last_ar_year, last_ar_reminder_year. Relationships: filings, offices, party_roles, share_classes, aliases, resolutions, documents, consent_continuation_outs, amalgamating_businesses, batch_processing, jurisdictions; submitter links to User. GOTCHA: identifier setter raises exception but caller must handle; no check before identifier assignment elsewhere in chunk.

structured.condensed:
Properties and methods on a Business model for filing and standing rules. 

`business_legal_name` hybrid property returns legal name: for firms (sole proprietors, partnerships), queries PartyRole (filtering PARTNER and PROPRIETOR roles where cessation_date is null), orders by name, returns concatenated names of first two parties with 'et al' if more exist; otherwise returns legal_name field. 

`is_firm` property returns true if legal_type is SOLE_PROP or PARTNERSHIP. 

`good_standing` property: firms are always in good standing; when 'enable_involuntary_dissolution' flag is on, checks _has_no_transition_filed_after_restoration() and returns false if true; for ACTIVE state businesses without restoration_expiry_date, compares (last_ar_date or founding_date) + 1 year 2 months 1 day against current UTC time; limited restoration sets it false; otherwise returns true.

`_has_no_transition_filed_after_restoration()` checks via subqueries: legal_type not EXTRA_PRO_A and founding_date before 2004-03-29, restoration filing exists (type RESTORATION or RESTORATIONAPPLICATION, status COMPLETED, effective_date + 1 year ≤ now), but no transition filing (type TRANSITION, status COMPLETED) between restoration effective_date and restoration effective_date + 1 year.

`next_anniversary` property returns (last_ar_date or founding_date) + 1 year.

`get_ar_dates(next_ar_year)` returns min/max dates for annual report: default Jan 1 to Dec 31; for COOP in 2020 extends max to Oct 31 next year (COVID), else Apr 30 next year; for CORPS sets min to founding_date + years elapsed, max to min + 60 days; caps max at today.

`mailing_address` and `delivery_address` properties query Office (registeredOffice, then businessOffice fallback for SP/GP), filter Address by type, fall back to direct Address query on business_id.

`in_dissolution` property queries BatchProcessing join Batch: matches business_id, BatchProcessing status not COMPLETED or WITHDRAWN, Batch status not COMPLETED, type INVOLUNTARY_DISSOLUTION; returns true if found.

`save()` adds to session and commits. `delete()` is a no-op unless dissolution_date exists (then saves); always returns self. This chunk shows no permission checks.

structured.condensed:
Returns alternate names and amalgamation status for a business in the Registry system.

`get_alternate_names()` returns a dict of alternate names: fetches active alias records with effective dates formatted as legislation dates; appends SP DBA entries (legal_type, identifier, legal_name, founding_date, start_date) when this business is not a sole proprietor, by querying businesses linked via Party and PartyRole where party_type is ORGANIZATION and role is PROPRIETOR; for firms (SP or GP), also appends this business's own record as a DBA entry. Returns empty list if no aliases or DBA entries exist.

`get_amalgamated_into()` returns Amalgamation revision JSON or None: checks if this business state is HISTORICAL, has a state_filing_id, and that filing is an amalgamation_application; if all true, retrieves and returns Amalgamation.get_revision_json(state_filing.transaction_id, state_filing.business_id). Returns None if business is not part of an amalgamation or if TING is active (putBackOn scenario).

`is_pending_amalgamating_business(business_identifier)` classmethod queries Filing records: filters where _status equals 'PAID', _filing_type equals 'amalgamationApplication', and filing_json['filing']['amalgamationApplication']['amalgamatingBusinesses'] contains the provided identifier; returns one filing or None. This chunk shows no check enforcing caller authority.

`generate_numbered_legal_name(legal_type, identifier)` classmethod returns numbered legal name string: validates legal_type exists in Business.BUSINESSES; selects numberedLegalNameSuffix from that dict; sets prefix to identifier[1:] for CONTINUE_IN types or identifier[2:] for others; returns formatted string. Returns None if legal_type not in BUSINESSES.

`get_next_value_from_sequence(business_type)` classmethod returns next sequence value: maps business_type 'CP' to 'business_identifier_coop' or 'FM' to 'business_identifier_sp_gp'; executes SELECT nextval(sequence_name) and returns scalar result. Returns None if type not in mapping.

`validate_identifier(identifier)` staticmethod validates identifier format: returns True for 'NR' prefix; validates regex pattern (CP|XCP|BC|C|FM)\\d{7}; parses last 7 digits and rejects if zero; returns False otherwise. All BC Reg entities use this PREFIX + 7 digit format.

Stores and retrieves NAICS (North American Industry Classification System) business structure records at a specific hierarchical level and version.

Immutable database table with UUID primary key (naics_key), indexed by code, year, version, level, and class_title. Each record holds a six-digit code, year, version, hierarchical_structure string, class_title (up to 150 chars), class_definition (up to 5100 chars), optional superscript, and one-to-many relationship to NaicsElement records.

Entry points: find_by_search_term (searches by text across class_title and linked element descriptions), find_by_code (retrieves by code and level, defaulting to level 5), find_by_naics_key (retrieves by UUID). No permission checks shown. find_by_search_term branches on has_exact_match_class_title_match: if true, runs get_exact_match_query which returns all examples for matching titles or only matching examples for non-matching titles; if false, runs get_non_exact_match_query which splits search_term by space and matches each word against element_description. Both queries filter to current NAICS_YEAR and NAICS_VERSION from config, level 5, and element_type in [ALL_EXAMPLES, ILLUSTRATIVE_EXAMPLES]. json property returns dict with naicsKey, code, year, version, classTitle, classDefinition, and nested naicsElements array. get_naics_config reads NAICS_YEAR and NAICS_VERSION integers from app config.

structured.condensed:
Database model and query service for review records linked to filings. Stores review metadata (status, dates, name reference) and serves filtered, sorted, paginated list queries.

Entry points: `save()` writes this Review to database immediately, with no permission check shown. `find_by_id(review_id)` returns Review by id or None; no check shown. `get_review(filing_id)` returns Review by filing id or None; no check shown. `get_paginated_reviews(review_filter, mapped_sort_by_column)` filters by review_filter (status list, start_date, end_date, start_effective_date, end_effective_date, nr_number, identifier, completing_party, submitted_sort_by, submitted_sort_order, page, limit) and sorts; returns dict with reviews list, page, limit, total; builds each as review.json merged with futureEffectiveDate (isoformat if Filing.effective_date > now(timezone.utc), else empty string).

Decisions: submission_date >= start_date if review_filter.start_date; submission_date <= end_date if review_filter.end_date; (effective_date > now AND effective_date >= start_date_fed) if review_filter.start_effective_date; (effective_date > now AND effective_date <= end_date_fed) if review_filter.end_effective_date; nr_number ilike filter if review_filter.nr_number; identifier ilike filter if review_filter.identifier; completing_party ilike filter if review_filter.completing_party; status in filter if review_filter.status; sort by effective_date (desc if submitted_sort_order=='true' else asc) if submitted_sort_by, else default sort by creation_date asc.

json property returns dict with id, nrNumber, identifier, completingParty, status (as .name), submissionDate (isoformat), creationDate (isoformat), filingId, results (list of result.json).

ReviewStatus enum: AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED, RESUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED.

Populates amalgamation filing data by extracting and enriching information about amalgamating businesses, their directors, offices, share classes, and resolutions for a business amalgamation application.

Entry point: `_set_amalgamating_businesses` and `_set_from_primary_or_holding_business_data` are private methods called during filing preparation; this chunk shows no permission check.

Input: filing dictionary with amalgamationApplication containing amalgamatingBusinesses and parties.

Flow in `_set_amalgamating_businesses`: iterates over amalgamating businesses, retrieves legal name from filing data or database, appends identifier and legal name to output list, writes to `filing['amalgamatingBusinesses']`.

Flow in `_set_from_primary_or_holding_business_data`: finds primary or holding business among amalgamating businesses; retrieves its versioned data if transaction_id exists, else queries current state. Copies director parties (active at effective_date or versioned), appends completing party from filing. Copies registered and records offices, share classes, and resolution dates into filing output structure.

Decision: if `self._filing.transaction_id` exists, fetches versioned historical data via VersionedBusinessDetailsService (used for TED dissolved businesses with court order, where TING is restored); otherwise queries current database state. Decision applies to directors, offices, share_classes, and resolutions retrieval.

GOTCHA: no null check on `primary_or_holding_business` before accessing properties; `next()` call finding primary/holding business raises StopIteration if none exists.

Service to render furnishing documents as PDFs via the Gotenberg API.

Inputs: business, furnishing, document_key (DISSOLUTION or DISSOLUTION_COVER), variant (default or mail). Entry point `get_pdf()` is public; this chunk shows no check. Calls Gotenberg at config key REPORT_API_GOTENBERG_URL + '/reports/render/single' with Bearer token from Google OAuth (audience at REPORT_API_GOTENBERG_AUDIENCE), sending reportName, template HTML, templateVars object, and static files; timeout 1800 seconds. Returns PDF content if status 200, else None. Template loaded from config REPORT_TEMPLATE_PATH, substitutes marked parts (common/v2/style, common/v2/styleMail, common/certificateRegistrarSignature). For DISSOLUTION documents: formats furnishing name, business identifier, last AR date (from furnishing or business founding), processed date; sets variant, title (with XPRO determining CANCELLATION vs DISSOLUTION); queries Address by furnishing ID and formats postal code; loads registrar info by processed_date or report_date; for non-EXTRA_PRO_A businesses, calls MrasService.get_jurisdictions() and filters EP registrations by AB/SK/MB. For DISSOLUTION_COVER, only name and date in filename. Errors logged, not retried. GOTCHA: response.status_code check does not distinguish failure types; None return on any non-200 silently fails rendering. GOTCHA: MrasService call has no check on returned jurisdictions being None/invalid.

Module wrapping calls to external services used by the API.

Entry point: `publish_event(business, event_type, data, subject, message_id)` — called by other parts of the system with no check shown. Publishes an event message to a NATS subject. Builds a CloudEvents-format payload with specversion '1.x-wip', the supplied event_type, a source URL from LEGAL_API_BASE_URL plus the business identifier, an id (supplied message_id or new uuid), current UTC timestamp, content type 'application/json', the business identifier, and the data dict. Sends the payload as JSON to the queue via `queue.publish_json()`.

If publishing fails, captures an error message to Sentry with 'error' level and logs the error with business.id and full traceback. The exception is swallowed; the function does not raise.

GOTCHA: no check on who may call `publish_event`; exceptions are caught and logged but not re-raised.

structured.condensed:
Authorizes and lists business filings available to a user based on business state, legal type, user role, and blockers.

**Entry points:** `is_allowed(business, state, filing_type, legal_type, jwt, sub_filing_type, filing_id)` — checks if a filing type is permitted; `get_allowable_actions(jwt, business)` — returns filing types and actions a user may perform; `get_allowed_filings(business, state, legal_type, jwt, is_ignore_draft_blockers)` — lists filings by role and state.

**Inputs:** Business object with state, legal_type, id, state_filing_id, admin_freeze, good_standing, in_dissolution; JWT token; filing_id; user JWT role (checked for STAFF_ROLE, SYSTEM_ROLE, COLIN_SVC_ROLE to grant "staff" role; else "general").

**Outputs:** Boolean (is_allowed); dict with filing submission link and filingTypes array; filingTypes list with name, displayName, feeCode, type (optional).

**Main flow:** `is_allowed` fetches filing by id, returns False if status not DRAFT or CHANGE_REQUESTED; blocks amalgamationApplication for legal types C/CBEN/CUL/CCC; matches filing_type against allowable filings from `get_allowed_filings`. `get_allowable_actions` returns all filings for competent authority (CA_SEARCH product), else calls `get_allowed_filings`; grants viewAll only to CA_SEARCH users. `get_allowed_filings` determines user_role, queries `get_allowable_filings_dict()` by role and state, filters by businessRequirement and legalTypes, checks blockers via `business_blocker_check()`.

**Blocker decisions:** `has_blocker()` returns True if any: business blocker exists (DEFAULT, BUSINESS_FROZEN, DRAFT_PENDING, NOT_IN_GOOD_STANDING, AMALGAMATING_BUSINESS, IN_DISSOLUTION); valid state filing missing; completed/future-effective filing exists; warning filing exists. `business_blocker_check()` sets flags: DRAFT_PENDING if incomplete filings exist (statuses PENDING/PENDING_CORRECTION/ERROR/PAID/DRAFT); BUSINESS_FROZEN if admin_freeze; NOT_IN_GOOD_STANDING if not good_standing; AMALGAMATING_BUSINESS if amalgamated_into; IN_DISSOLUTION if in_dissolution.

**Permission check:** is_allowed shows no check; other functions show no entry-point authorization enforcement.

**Gotcha:** is_allowed checks filing status but does not verify caller authorization to edit that filing. get_allowable_actions grants "viewAll" to any CA_SEARCH token holder without verifying role context. business_blocker_check treats DRAFT_PENDING and DEFAULT identically, conflating two concepts.

structured.condensed:
Validates business filing eligibility by checking blocker conditions in a filing management system.

Entry points: Six public functions check different blocker types. No authorization check shown. Functions `has_blocker_invalid_state_filing`, `has_blocker_completed_filing`, `has_blocker_future_effective_filing` each accept a `blocker_checks` dict and optionally a Business or Filing object; they parse filing type strings (format "type.subtype"), query Filing table by type pairs and status, and return boolean. `has_blocker_invalid_state_filing` returns True if state_filing matches any type in `invalidStateFilings` list. `has_blocker_completed_filing` returns True if count of found COMPLETED filings is less than count in `completedFilings` list. `has_blocker_future_effective_filing` returns True if any PENDING or PAID filing has effective_date > now (UTC). `has_filing_match` and `is_filing_type_match` are helpers matching filing_type and optional filing_sub_type. `has_blocker_warning_filing` deduplicates warning types and returns True if any match `warningTypes` list.

Authorization: `get_allowed` checks JWT for STAFF_ROLE, SYSTEM_ROLE, or COLIN_SVC_ROLE to assign 'staff' role (else 'general'); queries allowable filings dict by state and legal_type; builds filtered filing type list. `are_digital_credentials_allowed` decodes JWT, checks user exists via User.find_by_jwt_token, requires BCSC login_source, SOLE_PROP legal_type, and owner-operator status (verified by `is_self_registered_owner_operator` matching registration filing submitter_id and name fields). `is_self_registered_owner_operator` gets first proprietor and completing_party from PartyRole, compares lowercase first/last names (proprietor middle_initial appended to first name).

Product check: `has_product` queries cached `get_account_products` (600s TTL, keyed by account_id from header) calling auth API orgs/{account_id}/products, returns True if any product code matches and subscriptionStatus is ACTIVE.

GOTCHA: no permission check in blocker functions; JWT signature not verified in `are_digital_credentials_allowed`; name matching is case-insensitive but no accent/unicode handling shown; `get_account_products` caches None response.

Retrieves and formats historical versions of a business entity's name translations, resolutions, officers, and share classes as of a specified transaction ID in the revision history service.

Entry points: All methods are static utility functions, callable by any code; this chunk shows no permission check.

Main flow: Query versioned database tables (Alias, Resolution, Party, Address, ShareClass, ShareSeries) filtered by transaction_id, business_id, operation_type != 2 (exclusions), and date-range logic using end_transaction_id. Collect matching records up to the transaction ID, ordered by transaction_id, and transform each to JSON.

Key decisions:
- get_name_translations_before_revision: excludes operation_type 2; filters by type='TRANSLATION'
- get_resolution_dates_revision: filters resolution_type='SPECIAL'; includes records where end_transaction_id is null or > transaction_id
- party_role_revision_json: formats party role differently if is_ia_or_after (nested roles array vs. flat role field); uses capitalize-split for roleType and id
- party_revision_json: includes delivery and mailing addresses; falls back mailing to delivery if mailing_address_id absent; adds id field for diff detection
- address_revision_json: looks up country description via pycountry.countries.search_fuzzy; returns empty string for nullable fields

Reads: versioned tables (Alias, Resolution, Party, Address, ShareClass, ShareSeries versions) via db.session.query with transaction_id range filters. Reads pycountry.countries for country name lookup.

Outputs: dictionaries serialized to JSON with camelCase keys (streetAddress, appointmentDate, postalCode, etc.), ids included for diff detection.

GOTCHA: address_revision_json may crash if pycountry lookup fails on malformed country code; no try-catch shown. GOTCHA: party_revision_json includes 'id' for diff but may reference address_revision without null-check on result (addressed later in code).

structured.condensed:
Validates amalgamating businesses and party roles for a business amalgamation filing in BC Registries.

_validate_foreign_businesses checks a foreign corporation being amalgamated: staff only may validate foreign jurisdiction (BC region must be invalid, US region not required); if forming a BC ULC Company with any BC company present, returns error; if any ULC already exists, blocks foreign corporation; if foreign corporation marked as Primary or Holding role, returns error; non-staff callers always receive error that foreign corporations require staff approval.

_validate_lear_businesses checks a LEAR business by identifier: if not found, returns error; if found, checks it is not HISTORICAL, has no pending/draft/future-effective filings, and is not part of another future effective amalgamation; for non-staff callers, checks business is affiliated with their account (via AccountService.get_account_by_affiliated_identifier) and in good standing, else returns errors.

_validate_amalgamation_type validates role composition against amalgamation_type: regular requires 2+ amalgamating businesses with no holding or primary; horizontal requires 1 primary + 1+ amalgamating with no holding, and no foreign/extra-Pro businesses; vertical requires 1 holding + 1+ amalgamating with no primary. Returns error if conditions unmet.

_is_business_affliated queries AccountService for account orgs and checks if identifier's org id matches account_id.

_has_pending_filing checks Filing.get_filings_by_status for DRAFT, PENDING, or PAID status.

validate_party counts completing_parties and director_parties roles (case-insensitive, space-to-underscore normalization): regular amalgamation requires 1+ Director and 1+ Completing Party; vertical/horizontal require only 1+ Completing Party.

validate_amalgamation_court_order delegates to validate_court_order if courtOrder present.

structured.condensed:
Validates annual report filings for business entities in a corporate registry system.

Entry point `validate()` receives a business object and annual report JSON; checks if both exist (no check shown on caller), then delegates to `validate_ar_year()` and conditionally to `validate_agm_year()` if the business legal type is COOP or XPRO_LIM_PARTNR (determined by `requires_agm()`); returns an Error object or None.

`validate_ar_year()` extracts annualReportDate from `filing/annualReport/annualReportDate` via `get_date()`, then enforces four sequential checks: date must be valid, must not be in the future (compared to `datetime.utcnow().date()`), must not precede the last annual report or founding date (computed from `business.last_ar_year` or `business.founding_date.year`), and must be the next contiguous year (validated against `business.get_ar_dates(next_ar_year)`). Each violation returns a BAD_REQUEST error with the field path.

`validate_agm_year()` extracts annualReportDate, submission date from `filing/header/date`, and annualGeneralMeetingDate from `filing/annualReport/annualGeneralMeetingDate`. If the report year matches submission year and AGM date is missing, returns BAD_REQUEST. Two commented-out warning blocks check `business.last_agm_date` year against AR year with a one- or two-year offset but are disabled. Returns None if all checks pass.

GOTCHA: `validate_agm_year()` declares return type `Tuple[int, List[Dict]]` but always returns `Error` or `None`. GOTCHA: Two warning conditions checking dissolution risk are commented out with no explanation. GOTCHA: No external validation that business or annual_report came from an authorized user.

Validates a Change of Directors filing for a business by checking director addresses and effective date against incorporation date, prior filings, and current time.

Entry point: `validate(business, cod)` takes a Business object and filing dictionary, returns an Error if invalid or None if valid; this chunk shows no caller check. Collects errors from two validators: `validate_directors_addresses()` checks that each director's address contains a valid ISO-2 country code via `pycountry.countries.search_fuzzy(country)[0].alpha_2`, appending error with path `/filing/changeOfDirectors/directors/{idx}/{address_type}/addressCountry` on LookupError. `validate_effective_date()` parses the `filing/header/effectiveDate` ISO string, converts to UTC datetime, then to legislation timezone date, and verifies: not in future (compares `datetime.utcnow()`), not before `business.founding_date`, and not before the most recent prior Change of Directors filing retrieved via `Filing.get_most_recent_legal_filing(business.id, Filing.FILINGS['changeOfDirectors']['name'])`. Each violation appends a distinct error message. Returns all accumulated errors as HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST with message list, or None.

GOTCHA: `validate_effective_date()` returns a dict on missing effective date but a list otherwise, breaking type consistency.

structured.condensed: Configuration and wrapper for LaunchDarkly feature flags, enabling flag checks against a user. Initializes the feature flag client on app startup using either remote SDK (production) or local flags.json (non-production). Entry point `is_on(flag, user)` checks if a flag is enabled for a user; `value(flag, user)` retrieves the flag value. Both accept optional User object (falls back to anonymous user). Main flow: resolve client from app extensions, convert user to key dict, call `client.variation()`, return result. Decision: if user provided, use `_user_as_key()` (extracting sub, firstname, lastname from User); else use `_get_anonymous_user()` (key='anonymous'). If client unavailable or exception occurs during variation call, logs error and returns False. Init: `init_app()` builds Config with LD_SDK_KEY, optionally wrapping FileDataSource for local file-based flags, sets client in app.extensions. Teardown: `teardown()` closes client. GOTCHA: Any exception from `client.variation()` is caught broadly, logged, and returns False with no retry or escalation.

structured.condensed:
Generates and merges PDF documents for business furnishing service (notices, dissolutions). Takes furnishing records; outputs single or batch PDFs with cover sheet.

Entry point `get_furnishing_document(furnishing: Furnishing)` returns bytes—callable by any code with a Furnishing instance; this chunk shows no check. Entry point `get_merged_furnishing_document(furnishings: list)` returns bytes for batch; no check shown.

Flow: instantiate with optional document_key and variant; set report data (business, furnishing) on a ReportV2 instance; call `get_pdf()` to render. For batch: loop furnishings, collect PDFs, skip any that fail with error log. Build cover by setting `_report_data` dict with letterCount, reportDate formatted as COVER_REPORT_DATE_FORMAT, customBatchId from sequence, pageCount, ENV from config; render cover PDF. Merge all using PyPDF2.PdfFileMerger: append cover if present, append each content PDF, write to BytesIO buffer.

structured.condensed:
Determines which businesses are eligible for involuntary dissolution in the legal registry system.

Entry point `check_business_eligibility(identifier, eligibility_filters)` accepts a business identifier string and optional filters; any caller may invoke it. It queries businesses matching eligibility criteria and returns a tuple of (eligible: bool, eligibility_details: EligibilityDetails). Entry point `get_businesses_eligible(num_allowed)` returns all eligible businesses or a limited count; any caller may invoke it. Entry point `get_businesses_eligible_count()` returns the count of eligible businesses; any caller may invoke it. Entry point `get_in_dissolution_batch_processing(business_id)` fetches the active BatchProcessing record for a business undergoing involuntary dissolution; any caller may invoke it. This chunk shows no permission checks.

Eligibility requires: legal type in ELIGIBLE_TYPES (COMP, BC_ULC_COMPANY, BC_CCC, BCOMP, CONTINUE_IN, ULC_CONTINUE_IN, CCC_CONTINUE_IN, BCOMP_CONTINUE_IN, EXTRA_PRO_A, LIMITED_CO); business state is ACTIVE; admin_freeze is False; no_dissolution is False; not already in dissolution (by default, configurable); either ar_overdue or transition_overdue condition true. Decisions: `exclude_in_dissolution` (default True) excludes businesses with active BatchProcessing records in involuntary dissolution batches. `exclude_future_effective_filing` (default False) excludes businesses with pending future-effective filings. Excludes businesses with dissolution filing delays, limited restorations, or XPRO registrations from NWPTA.

ar_overdue: founding date, latest restoration/restorationapplication (completed), or last_ar_date plus 26 months is before now. transition_overdue: for non-EXTRA_PRO_A businesses founded before 2004-03-29, a restoration/restorationapplication filing exists (completed) but no transition filing completed within 12 months after it.

GOTCHA: no permission check on any entry point; no duplicate guard when marking business for dissolution; no retry logic shown for batch processing queries.

structured.condensed:
Helper functions that return SQLAlchemy filter clauses for business eligibility checks in a dissolution-related system.

Four fixed checks: `_has_future_effective_filing()` queries for pending or paid filings against the business, returning True if any exist. `_has_delay_of_dissolution_filing()` is unimplemented and always returns False. `_is_limited_restored()` checks if the business has a non-null restoration expiry date not yet passed (UTC timezone). `_is_xpro_from_nwpta()` checks if the business is extraprovincial from NWPTA jurisdictions (legal type EXTRA_PRO_A, Canada, foreign region in AB/SK/MB).

`_check_feature_flags_filter()` gates on the flag `enable-involuntary-dissolution-filter`. If off, returns True (no filter). If on, reads `involuntary-dissolution-filter` config (include-accounts and exclude-accounts lists). Calls `_get_filtered_entities()` on each account ID to fetch affiliations via `AccountService.get_affiliations()`, extracting business identifiers (excluding those starting with T or NR). Returns SQLAlchemy clauses: if only exclude list, excludes those identifiers; if only include list, includes those; if both, includes from the include list minus overlap with exclude. `_get_filtered_entities()` loops account IDs, fetches entity affiliations, filters by identifier pattern, returns the list. No checks enforce who calls these helpers. Filing queries and restoration date checks use UTC timezone function.

structured.condensed:
NameXService provides methods to query, validate, and update name requests in the namex-api, and to check for legal name changes in filings.

Entry points: `query_nr_number(identifier)` and `query_nr_numbers(identifiers)` are static methods (called by unspecified callers); this chunk shows no check. They fetch a single or multiple name requests from namex-api using a bearer token from AccountService. `update_nr(nr_json)` and `update_nr_as_future_effective(nr_json, future_effective_date)` are static methods (called by unspecified callers); this chunk shows no check. They authenticate to a separate Keycloak realm via `NAMEX_AUTH_SVC_URL` using `NAMEX_SERVICE_CLIENT_USERNAME` and `NAMEX_SERVICE_CLIENT_SECRET` config keys with client_credentials grant, then PUT the name request to namex-api at `NAMEX_SVC_URL + 'requests/' + nr_json['nrNum']`. `update_nr_as_future_effective` converts the date to GMT, adds 1 day as a processing buffer, sets `nr_json['expirationDate']` to that date in DATE_FORMAT, and calls `update_nr()`. `validate_nr(nr_json)` returns a dict with `is_consumable`, `is_approved`, `is_expired`, `consent_required`, `consent_received` based on `nr_json['state']` and `nr_json['consentFlag']`: if `disable-nr-check` flag is on, all checks are bypassed and it returns consumable=True, approved=True; otherwise if state is APPROVED, consumable and approved are True; if CONDITIONAL, approved is True, consent_required is True, and consent_received is True only if consentFlag is 'R', or consent_required is False if consentFlag is 'N' or absent—in both latter cases consumable is True; if EXPIRED, expired is True. `is_date_past_expiration(nr_json, date_time)` parses `nr_json['expirationDate']` using DATE_FORMAT or DATE_FORMAT_WITH_MILLISECONDS, converts to GMT, and returns True if it is before date_time. `get_approved_name(nr_json)` returns the name string from nr_json where the name's state matches the NR state (APPROVED or CONDITION for conditional NR), or None; if `disable-nr-check` is on, bypasses state check. `has_correction_changed_name(filing)` loads the corrected filing by ID from the database, extracts nrNumber and legalName from both filings' incorporation application name request paths, and returns whether either differs. No data is saved before any step; auth failures in update_nr return the auth response body; namex-api failures return the response. GOTCHA: query methods return raw HTTP response objects, not validated status. GOTCHA: update_nr swallows auth errors as a JSON dict but does not retry. GOTCHA: validate_nr returns different consent states for consentFlag absent (consent_required=False, is_consumable=True) vs 'N' (same), conflating two conditions.

Provides PDF manipulation and registrar certification stamping for legal documents. 

`PdfService.stamp_pdf` merges a watermark PDF onto an input PDF (first page only by default or all pages if `only_first_page=False`), combining pages with `PyPDF2.PdfFileReader` and `PyPDF2.PdfFileWriter`, returning a `BytesIO` buffer. `create_registrars_stamp` generates a single-page certification stamp as a `BytesIO` buffer: it retrieves registrar info for the given `certify_date` from `RegistrarInfo.get_registrar_info()`, draws a signature image at fixed margins (top-right), and writes text lines (BCSans font, 10pt) at fixed margins (left-center) showing the filed date (formatted by `LegislationDatetime.as_legislation_timezone` and `LegislationDatetime.format_as_report_string`), a "(Corrected)" suffix if `is_correction=True`, optional file name, and incorporation number—the date timezone conversion depends on the `LegislationDatetime` module's interpretation of `data.certify_date`. `_write_text` helper draws each line of text, decrementing y-margin by `line_height` for each. Entry point `stamp_pdf` is static and shows no permission check; `create_registrars_stamp` is a classmethod and shows no permission check. Loads BCSans font from `FONTS_PATH` config. GOTCHA: `PyPDF2.PdfFileReader` and `PyPDF2.PdfFileWriter` are deprecated in recent PyPDF2 versions; no error handling if font or registrar image file is missing.

structured.condensed: Flask extension that publishes JSON payloads to a NATS Streaming (STAN) queue. Reads Flask config for NATS_CLIENT_NAME, NATS_SERVERS, NATS_FILER_SUBJECT, NATS_CLUSTER_ID, and NATS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT. On init_app call, creates NATS and STAN client options with randomised client_id. Connects lazily on publish if not already connected, storing clients in Flask app context. publish_json (synchronous) and publish_json_to_subject/async_publish_json (asynchronous) both JSON-encode the payload, encode to UTF-8, and call stan.publish to the subject (defaulting to NATS_FILER_SUBJECT). Errors are logged and re-raised; no retry or idempotency guard. Teardown closes both clients on app context destruction. Exposes is_connected, is_closed, nats, and stan properties; four lifecycle callbacks (on_error, on_reconnect, on_disconnect, on_close) log warnings when triggered by NATS client. structured.condensed:
Checks involuntary dissolution eligibility for a business and returns warning messages if the business is ineligible to file or already in dissolution.

Entry point: `check_business(business: Business)` receives a Business object; this chunk shows no authorization check. Calls `InvoluntaryDissolutionService.check_business_eligibility()` with the business identifier and filters to exclude future-effective filings. If eligible, appends a warning for transition overdue or annual reports overdue. If not eligible, calls `InvoluntaryDissolutionService.get_in_dissolution_batch_processing(business.id)` to check if the business is already in dissolution. If in dissolution, determines target dissolution date via `_get_modified_warning_data()` and appends warnings for overdue filings plus a DISSOLUTION_IN_PROGRESS warning.

`_get_modified_warning_data(batch_processing)` reads `batch_processing.meta_data`, `batch_processing.trigger_date`, and `batch_processing.step`. Returns modified metadata dict. If step is WARNING_LEVEL_1, calculates `modified_target_date` as the maximum of current date and trigger date plus `STAGE_2_DELAY` config days. If step is WARNING_LEVEL_2, uses the maximum of current date and trigger date. Merges `targetDissolutionDate` (ISO format) into metadata.

Returns a list of warning dicts keyed by code, message, warningType, and optionally data. No explicit error handling, retries, or permission checks shown.

structured.condensed:
Utilities for CORS pre-flight handling and schema validation error formatting in an HTTP request framework.

`cors_preflight` is a decorator that adds an OPTIONS method to a decorated class. It accepts a `methods` parameter (default 'GET'), which is always returned as the Allow header regardless of the parameter value. The OPTIONS handler returns status 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*', Access-Control-Allow-Methods: (the methods parameter), and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: 'Authorization, Content-Type'. The decorator uses `setattr` to attach the options method to the decorated function.

`build_schema_error_response` reformats schema validation errors into a list. For each error, it extracts the path (joined with '/'), the error message, and iterates through error.context items to build a validation_errors list where each context item becomes an object with message, jsonPath, validator, and validatorValue fields. The function returns a list of objects with path, error, and context keys.

GOTCHA: the `methods` parameter to `cors_preflight` is ignored; the Allow header always returns 'GET' hardcoded.

A module containing Legal Filing processors that communicate with CRA to handle business entity changes. 

Incoming XML is built from Jinja2 templates by combining business entity data with lookups of business type/sub-type codes (mapped by legal_type and owner_legal_type, with defaults of '99' when type is unknown) and program codes from `program_type_code` dict ('SP'→'113', 'GP'→'114', 'BC'→'100', 'BEN'→'100', 'ULC'→'125', 'CC'→'126'). Document sub-types are set from `document_sub_type` dict ('CHANGE_PARTY'→'102', 'CHANGE_NAME'→'103', 'CHANGE_DELIVERY_ADDRESS'→'107', 'CHANGE_MAILING_ADDRESS'→'108'). Tax ID (BN15) is split into three components (businessRegistrationNumber [0:9], businessProgramIdentifier [9:11], businessProgramAccountReferenceNumber [11:15]) or returns empty strings if missing or wrong length. The input XML is sent via HTTP GET to BN_HUB_API_URL with Basic auth (BN_HUB_CLIENT_ID and BN_HUB_CLIENT_SECRET), returning status code and response text; network errors return None status and error string. For party changes before Business Number arrives, a hardcoded note instructs manual XML modification. Owner legal type is queried from local Business table or fallback to SEARCH_API /businesses/search/facets with status:ACTIVE filter; both return (legal_type, Business object or None), with None on any HTTP error. Events are published to NATS via QueueServiceManager. This chunk shows no permission checks.

structured.condensed:
Informs CRA via BN Hub about changes of business name and address from a filed change-of-registration request.

Entry point: `process(business, filing)` is called by the filing handler (no check shown). It detects changes: legal name change invokes `change_name` with CHANGE_NAME type; party name change invokes `change_name` with CHANGE_PARTY type; business office address changes invoke `change_address` with CHANGE_DELIVERY_ADDRESS or CHANGE_MAILING_ADDRESS type. For party name, it queries partners and proprietors (non-ceased) sorted by trimmed concatenated name and takes first 2 as comma-joined string, appending ", et al" if more exist.

`change_name` and `change_address` follow the same pattern: query RequestTracker by business, service (BN_HUB), request type, and filing; create new tracker if absent or increment retry_number and update last_modified if existing and not processed. Exit early if already processed. Build XML payload via `build_input_xml` with retry number, filing ID, document sub-type code, client name/address type code, update reason code, new name or effective date and address, business JSON, and split tax ID. Store payload in request_object. If tax_id missing or not 15 characters, set response_object to bn_note and save without calling BN Hub. Processes a dissolution or putBackOn filing status change request for a sole proprietor or general partnership, coordinating with the BN Hub service.

Entry point: `process(business, filing)` is called by the filing system when a dissolution or putBackOn filing is submitted; this chunk shows no check. The function retrieves or creates a `RequestTracker` to track retries; on retry, it increments `retry_number` and updates `last_modified`. If already processed (`is_processed` is True), it returns early.

Flow: Converts the filing's `effective_date` to legislation timezone in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Maps filing type to program account codes: 'putBackOn' → status '01' with reason None; 'dissolution' → status '02' with reason '105'. Builds XML payload via `build_input_xml('change_status', {...})` containing retry number, filing ID, status/reason codes, effective date, business JSON, and split tax ID components. Saves payload to `request_tracker.request_object`.

Validation: If `business.tax_id` is missing or not exactly 15 characters, sets `response_object` to `bn_note`, saves, and returns without calling BN Hub.

Request: Calls `request_bn_hub(input_xml)` to POST to external BN Hub service with XML credentials embedded. On HTTP 200, parses XML response; if root tag is 'SBNAcknowledgement', sets `is_processed` to True. Always saves `response_object` and tracker state.

Failure handling: If not processed and `retry_number < max_retry`, raises `BNException` to trigger retry. If retries exhausted, raises `BNRetryExceededException` to fail permanently. Parsing errors are suppressed; no duplicate guard exists.

GOTCHA: Parse errors are silently suppressed (`suppress(Et.ParseError)`), so malformed responses mark as unprocessed without logging.

Processes business registration with the CRA by orchestrating two sequential requests: INFORM_CRA to notify CRA, then GET_BN to retrieve the business number, with retry logic and email notifications.

Entry point: `process(business, is_admin, msg, skip_build)` — called by queue handler for admin requests (checked via `is_admin` flag; admin requests require `msg` parameter or raise QueueException) or normal processing when business has 9-digit `tax_id`. 

Flow: (1) Retrieves or creates RequestTracker for INFORM_CRA request; increments retry counter on retries; (2) calls `_inform_cra()` to send XML registration data to BN_HUB; (3) if not processed and retries remain, raises BNException; if retries exhausted, raises BNRetryExceededException; (4) parses response XML to extract `transactionID`; (5) retrieves or creates RequestTracker for GET_BN request with that transaction ID; (6) calls `_get_bn()` to poll for business number; (7) on failure, raises BNException or BNRetryExceededException; (8) publishes email event via `publish_event()` with type 'businessNumber' and config key `EMAIL_PUBLISH_OPTIONS.subject`; (9) publishes subscription notification event via `publish_event()` with CloudEvents format to config key `SUBSCRIPTION_OPTIONS.subject`.

Conditions: `skip_build=True` skips retry (returns early on failure); `is_admin=True` uses `msg.data.header.businessNumber` instead of `business.tax_id`.

State: RequestTracker records before each network call, with `is_processed`, `retry_number`, `last_modified`, `response_object`, and `message_id` fields.

GOTCHA: Email and subscription publish failures are caught broadly and logged, then re-raised, but both succeed silently before RequestTracker is saved — if database write fails between publish calls and commit, events are published but tracker not recorded. Admin resubmit with `skip_build=True` fails immediately without retry.

structured.condensed:
Informs CRA (Canada Revenue Agency) of a new business registration and retrieves the assigned business number, in a business filing system.

Entry points: `_inform_cra` (called by unknown, shows no check), `_get_bn` (called by unknown, shows no check), `_get_program_account` (called by unknown, shows no check).

`_inform_cra` takes Business, RequestTracker, business_number string, and skip_build flag. If request_tracker.is_processed is true, returns early. If skip_build is false, builds XML input: extracts business legal type (checking if FIRMS or CORPS), constructs legal_names and parties list (for FIRMS, sorts partners/proprietors by trimmed name, takes up to 5 for XML, handles SP owned by GP by fetching owner legal_name from get_owners_legal_type), looks up founding_date in legislation timezone, retrieves directors for CORPS, calls get_business_type_and_sub_type_code with legal_type, business_owned, owner_legal_type flags. Creates retry_number by appending request_tracker.message_id if present. Calls build_input_xml with 'create_program_account_request' and dictionary containing business identifier/name/naics, programTypeCode from program_type_code dict, founding_date, legal_names, parties json slice [:5], addresses via .one_or_none().json, and boolean flags. Sends XML to request_bn_hub; if status code is OK, parses response as XML—if root tag is 'SBNAcknowledgement', sets is_processed true. Saves request_object as input_xml and response_object as response string to RequestTracker.

`_get_bn` checks request_tracker.is_processed, returns early if true. Sets request_object to business.identifier/transaction_id string. Calls _get_program_account. If status OK, extracts program_account_ref_no (zero-filled to 4 digits), concatenates business_no + business_program_id + program_account_ref_no into bn15, saves as business.tax_id, sets is_processed true. Saves response_object as JSON string to RequestTracker.

`_get_program_account` calls AccountService.get_bearer_token(), constructs URL to COLIN_API /programAccount/{identifier}/{transaction_id}, sends GET with CONTENT_TYPE_JSON headers and Bearer token authorization. Returns status_code and response.json(). On RequestException, logs error and returns None, error string.

GOTCHA: _inform_cra silently ignores parse errors (Et.ParseError suppressed); is_processed only set on valid XML acknowledgement, not on successful HTTP OK without acknowledgement tag. GOTCHA: _get_program_account returns (None, str_error) on exception but no retry; callers must handle None status_code. GOTCHA: _inform_cra has no transactional guarantee—request_object saved before response received, partial state if save fails after request_bn_hub but before response_object save. GOTCHA: No duplicate prevention; running _inform_cra twice with same data produces duplicate CRA requests.

NATS Streaming subscriber that processes CRA business filing events and routes them to specialized handlers.

Entry point: `cb_subscription_handler`, called by NATS Streaming when message arrives on subscription—this chunk shows no check on caller identity.

Receives: JSON message from NATS with `data` field containing event. Filters on `type` field: accepts only `bc.registry.business.registration`, `bc.registry.business.changeOfRegistration`, `bc.registry.business.correction`, `bc.registry.business.dissolution`, `bc.registry.business.putBackOn`, or `bc.registry.admin.bn`; returns null for others.

Flow: Decodes message, calls `process_event`. If type is `bc.registry.admin.bn`, routes to `admin.process(msg)` and returns. Otherwise, retrieves filing by ID from `msg['data']['filing']['header']['filingId']`; raises `QueueException` if not found. Retrieves business by `filing_submission.business_id`; raises `QueueException` if not found. Routes to handler based on `filing_submission.filing_type`: `registration.process(business)` for REGISTRATION; `change_of_registration.process(business, filing)` for CHANGEOFREGISTRATION; `correction.process(business, filing)` for CORRECTION only if business legal type is SOLE_PROP or PARTNERSHIP; `dissolution_or_put_back_on.process(business, filing)` for DISSOLUTION or PUTBACKON only if business legal type is SOLE_PROP or PARTNERSHIP.

Error handling: `OperationalError` (database down) re-raised; `BNException` re-raised; `BNRetryExceededException` logged only; other exceptions logged and sent to Sentry, then caught and handled. Message removed from queue regardless of error outcome.

GOTCHA: No transactionality; filing and business retrieved but may be modified between fetch and handler call. GOTCHA: `BNRetryExceededException` swallowed with log-only, no re-raise. GOTCHA: Broad `Exception` catch at end masks unexpected errors.

structured.condensed: Helper functions for issuing, revoking, and replacing digital credentials for businesses. Entry points are four public functions callable by any external code. `get_issued_digital_credentials` retrieves issued credentials for a business given its active DCConnection; returns empty list if connection or credentials not found. `issue_digital_credential` looks up or creates a DCDefinition by credential_type, retrieves the active connection, calls `DigitalCredentialsHelpers.get_digital_credential_data` to build credential payload, calls `digital_credentials.issue_credential` with connection_id, definition, and data, then saves a DCIssuedCredential record with the returned cred_ex_id and extracted credential_id. `revoke_issued_digital_credential` checks issued_credential.is_issued and not is_revoked, calls `digital_credentials.revoke_credential` with connection, revocation IDs, and reason, then sets is_revoked=True and saves. `replace_issued_digital_credential` revokes the old credential if issued, removes its credential_exchange_record, looks up the associated User via DCIssuedBusinessUserCredential.credential_id, deletes the issued_credential record, and calls `issue_digital_credential` with the new credential_type. All entry points show no permission check. All functions catch and re-raise exceptions; only the top-level caller logs or handles them. GOTCHA: all four functions re-raise caught exceptions without logging or recording failure state—caller must handle. GOTCHA: `replace_issued_digital_credential` does not guard against race conditions between revoke, remove, and delete operations.

NATS Streaming message handler for entity digital credentials: processes messages from a queue to revoke or reissue business credentials upon business number changes, administrative updates, or filing completions.

Entry point **cb_subscription_handler** is called by NATS Streaming when a message arrives; this chunk shows no check on the caller. It decodes JSON from the message, passes it to **process_digital_credential**.

**process_digital_credential** reads the message `type` field and routes by filing type. It permits five types: `bc.registry.business.bn`, `bc.registry.business.changeofregistration`, `bc.registry.business.dissolution`, `bc.registry.business.putbackon`, `bc.registry.admin.revoke`; rejects all others and returns None. For BN and REVOKE types, it reads `identifier` from the message (raises QueueException if missing), looks up the Business by identifier in the database, then calls **business_number.process()** or **admin_revoke.process()**. For the three filing types, it extracts `filingId` from `data.filing.header` (raises QueueException if missing), fetches the FilingCore by id and its `.storage` object (raises QueueException if not found), checks that `filing.status` equals `COMPLETED` (raises QueueException if not), looks up Business by `filing.business_id` (raises Exception if not found), then calls the matching processor: **change_of_registration.process(business, filing)**, **dissolution.process(business, filing_sub_type)**, or **put_back_on.process(business)**.

On OperationalError (database down), the exception is re-raised to leave the message in queue. On QueueException or any other Exception, the error is logged and the message is removed from the queue.

GOTCHA: The code catches and suppresses all exceptions except OperationalError, removing messages from the queue even when they fail.

structured.condensed:
Module providing email processor functions for entity filings: retrieves filing and business data, determines email recipients, fetches contact information from authentication service, substitutes template parts, and retrieves filing documents.

Entry points: `get_filing_info()` takes filing_id, queries Filing and Business tables, converts filing_date and effective_date from UTC to Pacific time as formatted strings; `get_recipients()` takes option, filing_json, optional token and filing_type ('incorporationApplication' default), extracts contactPoint email and Completing Party email if option is Filing.Status.PAID or 'bn' and header name matches filing_type, else queries auth service; `get_recipient_from_auth()` takes identifier and token, calls AUTH_URL/entities/{identifier} with Bearer token, returns first contact email, logs error and raises Exception if empty; `get_user_email_from_auth()` and `get_user_from_auth()` call AUTH_URL/users/{user_name} with Bearer token, return email from contacts or fallback field; `get_account_by_affiliated_identifier()` calls AUTH_URL/orgs?affiliation={identifier} with Bearer token, returns parsed JSON or None on exception; `get_org_id_for_temp_identifier()` extracts org id from account response; `get_entity_dashboard_url()` returns AUTH_WEB_URL/account/{org_id}/business for temp identifiers (starting 'T'), else DASHBOARD_URL + identifier; `substitute_template_parts()` takes template_code, reads 23 named template parts from TEMPLATE_PATH/common/ and replaces [[partname.html]] markers; `get_jurisdictions()` calls LEGAL_API_URL/mras/{identifier} with Bearer token, returns parsed JSON if status OK, None on failure; `get_filing_document()` calls LEGAL_API_URL/businesses/{business_identifier}/filings/{filing_id}/documents/{document_type} with Bearer token requesting PDF, base64-encodes and returns content or None on non-OK status or exception. This chunk shows no permission checks. GOTCHA: `get_recipient_from_auth()` raises bare Exception with no message; `get_account_by_affiliated_identifier()` and `get_filing_document()` catch all exceptions silently; `substitute_template_parts()` reads template files without verifying they exist.

Builds and sends email notification when an Affiliation filing is created or modified in BCRegistry.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` is called by an external handler with filing data and authorization token; this chunk shows no permission check. Retrieves filing details (type, status, effective date) by `get_filing_info()` via filingId from email_info. Reads template `BC-ALT-DRAFT.html` from `TEMPLATE_PATH` config, substitutes parts, and renders via Jinja2 with filing, business, header, dates, and dashboard URL built from `DASHBOARD_URL` config plus business identifier. Extracts recipients via `get_recipients(status, filing_json, token)`; if empty, returns empty dict. Constructs email with subject line `{legalName} - How to use BCRegistry.ca`, sender `BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca`, and rendered HTML body. Filing type display name is formatted by uppercasing first letter and splitting camelCase. Returns dict with recipients, requestBy, and content (subject and body).

GOTCHA: If `get_recipients()` returns empty, process returns empty dict instead of raising or logging the condition.

Builds email notification for an AGM Extension filing approval: retrieves filing data, formats HTML template, attaches AGM extension letter PDF and receipt PDF, identifies recipients, and returns email payload with subject, body and attachments.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` called by the email processor system to build AGM Extension notification emails. This chunk shows no check.

Flow: retrieves filing by `email_info['filingId']`; reads template `AGM-EXT-{status}.html` from disk; renders Jinja2 template with business name, filing data, header, dates, dashboard URL, filing type; calls `_get_pdfs()` to assemble attachments; calls `get_recipient_from_auth(identifier, token)` to fetch recipient email; deduplicates and joins recipients; constructs subject line, prefixed with legal name if not a numbered company; returns dict with recipients, requestBy='BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca', and content object containing subject, HTML body, and PDF attachments.

`_get_pdfs(token, business, filing, filing_date_time, effective_date)` fetches and encodes two PDF attachments: calls `get_filing_document()` to retrieve 'letterOfAgmExtension' PDF; POSTs to `PAY_API_URL/{filing.payment_token}/receipts` with corpName, dates, filingIdentifier, businessNumber, Authorization Bearer token, receives receipt PDF. Logs error if receipt POST returns non-201 status but continues without raising. Base64-encodes both PDFs, wraps each with fileName, fileBytes (utf-8 decoded), fileUrl (empty), attachOrder (sequential string).

GOTCHA: Receipt fetch failure is logged but not re-raised; email still succeeds without receipt. GOTCHA: fileUrl left empty string; unclear if downstream expects populated URL or handles empty gracefully.

structured.condensed:
Builds an email notification for an AGM Location Change filing in the business registry.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` receives an email info dict with `type`, `option` (status), and `filingId`; this chunk shows no check. Calls `get_filing_info` to fetch the filing, business, and localized dates. Loads an HTML template from `TEMPLATE_PATH/AGM-LOCCHG-{status}.html`, substitutes parts, and renders it via Jinja2 with business, filing, header, dates, dashboard URL, and filing type. Fetches PDF attachments via `_get_pdfs`: requests a filing PDF (type `letterOfAgmLocationChange`) via `get_filing_document`; if present, appends it as "Letter of AGM Location Change Approval.pdf". Posts to PAY_API_URL with the payment token to generate a receipt PDF, passing corpName, filingDateTime, effectiveDateTime (empty if same as filing date), filingIdentifier, and businessNumber (tax_id or empty); logs error if status is not 201, else appends receipt as "Receipt.pdf". Deduplicates recipients from `get_recipient_from_auth`, joins them comma-separated. Returns a dict with recipients, requestBy (hardcoded "BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca"), and content holding subject (formatted as "{legal name} - AGM Location Change Documents from the Business Registry" or "Numbered Company" if name starts with identifier), body (HTML), and attachments (PDF list ordered by attachOrder).

GOTCHA: Receipt generation returns only a logged error on failure; the email proceeds without it. GOTCHA: effectiveDateTime is omitted from the receipt request (sent as empty string) when it equals filingDateTime, which may create inconsistency if a consumer expects the field.

Builds and returns an email notification for an amalgamation filing event in the legal entity system.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` receives calls from the email notification workflow; this chunk shows no check. Takes filing ID from email_info, retrieves the filing record and business details. For PAID status, uses the temporary registration number and retrieves the primary or holding business legal name from filing data. For COMPLETED status, uses stored business data. Renders an HTML email template with filing details, filing date, effective date, business info, entity dashboard URL, and filing type. Calls `_get_pdfs` to attach documents: on PAID status, fetches the amalgamation application PDF and requests a receipt PDF from the payment service; on COMPLETED status, fetches the certificate of amalgamation PDF and notice of articles PDF. Each PDF is base64-encoded and appended with sequential attachment order. Calls `get_recipients` to retrieve email recipients from filing data; returns empty dict if none found. Sets email subject: "business legalName - Amalgamation" for PAID, "business legalName - Confirmation of Amalgamation" for COMPLETED. Returns dict with recipients, requestBy: 'BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca', and content object containing subject, HTML body, and PDF attachments.

Receipt PDF retrieval on status 201: if payment service returns non-201, logs error and skips receipt attachment—no retry or exception raised. No duplicate guard on recipients or attachments.

structured.condensed:
Builds and returns an email notification for a Change of Registration filing, in the email processor for the BC Business Registry.

Entry point: `process(email_info: dict, token: str)` receives filing ID, type, and status from the email queue. This chunk shows no permission check.

Flow: Retrieves filing data via `get_filing_info()`. Loads an HTML template named `CHGREG-{status}.html` from `TEMPLATE_PATH`, substitutes parts, and renders it with Jinja2 using business, filing, header, dates, dashboard URL, and filing type. Retrieves PDF attachments via `_get_pdfs()` based on status. Extracts recipients from changeOfRegistration parties with roles in ('Partner', 'Proprietor', 'Completing Party'), contactPoint email, and submitter email—via `get_user_email_from_auth()` for non-staff or `documentOptionalEmail` for staff in `filing.submitter_roles`. Deduplicates and joins recipients.

Decisions: If status is `Filing.Status.PAID.value`, subject is "Confirmation of Filing from the Business Registry" and PDF calls `get_filing_document()` with type 'changeOfRegistration'; then POSTs to `PAY_API_URL/{filing.payment_token}/receipts` with corpName, filingDateTime, effectiveDateTime (omitted if equal to filing date), filingIdentifier, businessNumber (from `Business.find_by_internal_id(filing.business_id).tax_id`), headers with bearer token. If receipt status is not 201, logs error but does not retry. If status is `Filing.Status.COMPLETED.value`, PDF type is 'amendedRegistrationStatement'. If legal name exists, prepends to subject.

Returns dict with recipients, requestBy 'BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca', content object containing subject, body HTML, and attachments (each with fileName, fileBytes base64-decoded to UTF-8 string, fileUrl empty, attachOrder string).

GOTCHA: Receipt fetch failure is logged but does not stop email send. GOTCHA: `documentOptionalEmail` is added to recipients unconditionally for non-staff; no check that it is populated.

structured.condensed:
Builds an email notification for a Continuation In filing in the Business Registry, with receipt or certificate attachments depending on filing status.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` — called by the email processor to build the notification; this chunk shows no check. Receives email_info dict with filing_id, type, option (status); retrieves filing details via `get_filing_info()`, extracts business and filing data from the filing JSON. For PAID status, substitutes the nameRequest business from filing_data. Fetches the foreign jurisdiction name by looking up country and region codes in pycountry. Loads template `CONT-IN-{status}.html` from TEMPLATE_PATH config, substitutes template parts, renders with Jinja2 passing business, filing_data, dates, entity_dashboard_url, filing_name, numbered_description, foreign_jurisdiction, and latest_review_comment (fetched from ReviewResult, with newlines encoded). Calls `_get_pdfs()` to gather attachments: for PAID, fetches 'continuationIn' PDF and posts to PAY_API_URL with payment_token to generate receipt (logs error if status != 201, does not retry); for RESUBMITTED, fetches 'continuationIn' PDF; for COMPLETED, fetches 'certificateOfContinuation' and 'noticeOfArticles' PDFs. Calls `get_recipients()` to get email recipients; returns empty dict if none. Assigns subject based on status. Returns dict with recipients, requestBy 'BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca', and content (subject, HTML body, PDF attachments).

GOTCHA: Receipt generation to PAY_API_URL is not retried on failure, only logged. GOTCHA: No check that filing exists or is valid before processing. GOTCHA: ReviewResult comment encoding and HTML decoding of newlines could cause display issues if comment contains literal '\n' strings.

Assembles and returns a list of PDF attachments for dissolution application email notifications.

Entry point: `_get_pdfs(status, token, business, filing, filing_date_time, effective_date)` — called from elsewhere in the email processor; this chunk shows no check.

Flow branches on `status`: if `Filing.Status.PAID.value`, skips PDF for legal types 'SP' or 'GP', calls `get_filing_document(business['identifier'], filing.id, 'voluntaryDissolution', token)` for others and appends to `pdfs` if returned; posts to `PAY_API_URL/{filing.payment_token}/receipts` with `corpName`, `filingDateTime`, `effectiveDateTime` (omitted if equal to `filingDateTime`), `filingIdentifier`, and `businessNumber` (from `business_data.tax_id` or empty), headers with `Authorization: Bearer {token}`; logs error if status code is not 201, else base64-encodes response content and appends as 'Receipt.pdf'. If `Filing.Status.COMPLETED.value`, for legal types 'SP' or 'GP' gets 'dissolution' PDF and appends as 'Statement of Dissolution.pdf'; for others, if `filing.filing_sub_type != 'administrative'` gets 'certificateOfDissolution' and appends; if `legal_type == Business.LegalTypes.COOP.value` also gets 'affidavit' and 'specialResolution' PDFs and appends. Each PDF dict holds `fileName`, `fileBytes` (base64-decoded string), `fileUrl` (empty), and `attachOrder` (string). Returns `pdfs` list.

GOTCHA: receipt POST failure is logged but does not halt — email may send without receipt if PAY_API unreachable or returns error.

Builds the email notification for a Business Registry dissolution filing. Entry point is `process(email_info, token)`, callable by a dissolution notification handler with no check shown. Inputs: email_info dict with keys `type`, `option`, `filingId`; token string. Outputs: dict with `recipients` (comma-separated emails), `requestBy` (BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca), `content` (subject, body HTML, attachments list).

Flow: retrieves filing, business, and filing dates via `get_filing_info(filingId)`; reads template from config path `TEMPLATE_PATH/DIS-{status}.html`; substitutes template parts and renders Jinja template with business, filing, header, dates, dashboard URL, filing name, and type; calls `_get_pdfs(status, token, business, filing, dates)` for attachments; builds recipients list by calling `get_recipient_from_auth(identifier, token)` and conditionally `get_user_email_from_auth(submitter.username, token)`. Decisions: if status is PAID and legal_type in [SP, GP], subject is "Confirmation of Filing from the Business Registry", else "Voluntary dissolution"; if status is COMPLETED and legal_type in [SP, GP], subject is "Dissolution Documents from the Business Registry", else "Confirmation of Dissolution from the Business Registry"; fallback subject is "Notification from the BC Business Registry". If legal_type is SP or GP, adds all party and party_role emails; else adds only Custodian role emails. Deduplicates and filters null recipients.

GOTCHA: no check shown for caller authorization; no check shown for token validity; subject assignment uses uninitialized `subject` variable with fallback only after conditionals.

Builds and sends email notification for stage 1 involuntary dissolution (overdue annual report or transition report), attaching a PDF furnishing document.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` — called by email queue handler with furnishing ID. No check shown. Reads furnishing and business from database. Loads HTML template from `TEMPLATE_PATH/INVOL-DIS-STAGE-1.html`, substitutes template parts, renders with Jinja2 using business JSON, dashboard URL, extra-provincial jurisdictions (Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Saskatchewan only), and furnishing type. For non-XPRO furnishing types, calls `get_jurisdictions()` to populate extra-provincials list; XPRO types skip this. Recipient is furnishing email address. Subject is "Attention {identifier} - {legal_name}". Calls `_get_pdfs()` to fetch furnishing PDF from legal API via bearer token; returns empty list on HTTP error (logged) or unrecognized furnishing type. PDF filename is "Notice of Commencement of Cancellation.pdf" for XPRO types, else "Notice of Commencement of Dissolution.pdf". Encodes PDF as base64, returns in attachments array.

Entry point: `post_process(email_msg, status)` — called after email send with PROCESSED or FAILED status. No check shown. Updates furnishing record with status, processed_date, last_modified timestamp; if FAILED, adds note 'Failure to send email'. Saves to database.

`PROCESSABLE_FURNISHING_NAMES` constant lists four furnishing types that trigger PDF fetch: `DISSOLUTION_COMMENCEMENT_NO_AR`, `DISSOLUTION_COMMENCEMENT_NO_TR`, and their `_XPRO` variants.

GOTCHA: No permission or authorization check on entry points. No retry on PDF fetch failure — returns empty list and logs error only.

structured.condensed:
Processes notification emails for a Registration Application filing in the BC Business Registry. Receives a filing ID, status (PAID or COMPLETED), and auth token. Retrieves the filing and business data, fetches a Receipt PDF (if PAID) or Statement of Registration PDF (if COMPLETED), and determines recipients based on filing roles: Completing Party always; if COMPLETED, add contact point email and all Partners or Proprietors. Builds an email via Jinja template (REG-{status}.html) with filing details, effective date, entity dashboard URL and corp type description. Returns recipients, sender (BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca), subject line (filing legal name plus "Confirmation of Filing" if PAID, "Registration Documents" if COMPLETED), rendered HTML body, and PDF attachments with order number.

Entry point: `process(email_info, token)` — called by the email processor; chunk shows no permission check.

Calls: PAY_API_URL to POST /[filing.payment_token]/receipts with corpName, filingDateTime, effectiveDateTime, filingIdentifier, businessNumber, and Bearer token in Authorization header — returns PDF binary or HTTP error, logged if status is not 201. Calls `get_filing_document()` with identifier, filing ID, 'registration', and token to fetch Statement PDF. Calls `get_filing_info()` to read filing, business, leg_tmz_filing_date, leg_tmz_effective_date from filing ID. Calls `get_entity_dashboard_url()` to read entity URL. Calls `CorpType.find_by_id()` to read corp type. Reads filing JSON for registration data, parties, and contact point. Reads TEMPLATE_PATH config and REG-{status}.html template.

structured.condensed: Builds email notifications for Restoration Application filings in the Business Registry when paid or completed. Entry point is `process(email_info, token)` called by an external notification handler; this chunk shows no check. Takes filing ID, type ('restoration'), and status ('PAID' or 'COMPLETED') from email_info. Selects Jinja2 template by restoration type and status (e.g., 'RES-fullRestoration-PAID.jinja2' falling back to 'RES-PAID.jinja2'), renders it with business, filing, and timestamp data. Fetches filing documents via `get_filing_document` (Notice of Articles, Certificate of Restoration if COMPLETED; Restoration Application if PAID). Generates subject line conditionally: 'Confirmation of Filing from the Business Registry' if PAID, 'Restoration Documents from the Business Registry' if COMPLETED, or fallback 'Notification from the BC Business Registry'. Prepends legal name to subject. Returns dict with recipients (comma-separated), requestBy='BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca', and content (subject, body as rendered HTML, attachments as PDF array with fileName, fileBytes, fileUrl, attachOrder). GOTCHA: if PAY_API_URL receipt request fails, the error is only logged; no retry, no exception raised, and PAID status may return without receipt PDF.

Renders a business information table for filing confirmations in a document template, showing company name (conditional on legal type), registration or incorporation number, business tax ID if present, and filing timestamp, with effective date if future-effective.

Inputs: `business` object with `legalType`, `legalName`, `identifier`, `taxId`; `filing` object with nested `nameRequest.legalName`; `filing_status`, `filing_type`, `filing_date_time`, `effective_date_time`, `numbered_description`, `header.isFutureEffective`. Outputs: rendered HTML table rows with key-value pairs.

Flow: Label changes based on business `legalType` (Cooperative/Sole Proprietor or General Partnership/Corporation). For PAID filings of amalgamationApplication, continuationIn, or incorporationApplication, displays legal name from `filing.nameRequest.legalName`, falling back to `numbered_description`, else "Unknown". Otherwise displays `business.legalName`. Registration/incorporation number shows "Pending" for PAID incorporationApplication, else `business.identifier`. Includes `business.taxId` row only if present and longer than 9 characters. Always includes filing date-time; includes effective date-time row only if `header.isFutureEffective` is true.

GOTCHA: No validation that `business.taxId` length check (>9) correctly identifies valid business numbers; fallback to "Unknown" occurs silently without logging why name resolution failed.

A Jinja2 template that renders a business information section for a filing confirmation document. It displays the business name (labeled based on legal type: Cooperative Association Name for CP, Business Name for SP/GP, Company Name for others), registration or incorporation number (with "Pending" for paid incorporation applications, otherwise the identifier), business tax ID if present and longer than 9 characters, filing date and time, and effective date and time if the filing is future effective.

**Decision logic:**
- Business name label depends on `business.legalType` being 'CP', 'SP'/'GP', or other
- Business name value: if filing is PAID incorporationApplication, attempts `filing.nameRequest.legalName`, falls back to `numbered_description`, then "Unknown"; otherwise uses `business.legalName`
- Registration/Incorporation number label depends on `business.legalType` being 'SP'/'GP' or other
- Registration/Incorporation number value: "Pending" if filing is PAID incorporationApplication, otherwise `business.identifier`
- Tax ID renders only if `business.taxId` exists and length > 9
- Effective date section renders only if `header.isFutureEffective` is true

All fields are conditionally rendered; template includes spacing and divider includes.

structured.condensed: Service that creates, retrieves, and updates MessageProcessing records tracking incoming messages through their status lifecycle. Creates MessageProcessing with message_id, source, identifier, message_type, status, message JSON, seen count, and error—all persisted with UTC timestamps. Updates status by message object or by message_id, optionally incrementing seen count and storing error details; seen count increments are guarded by a flag but persist immediately via save(). Retrieves messages by message_id alone or by source+message_id pair. Four update methods—update_message_status, update_message_status_by_message_id, update_message_last_error—all write immediately to the database without transaction wrapper or rollback guard; seen_count increments are non-atomic. GOTCHA: update_message_status accepts error_details parameter typed as None with no-op condition, making it unreachable; update_message_status_by_message_id has no error_details field despite similar purpose.

All changes are direct model mutations. Does not save or commit.

structured.condensed: Flask application factory and initialization for the Authorization API service. Entry point: `create_app(run_mode)` creates and configures the Flask app from environment or `FLASK_ENV` parameter, reading settings from `config.CONFIGURATION[run_mode]`. Flow: initializes database (db, ma), mail, Sentry (if `SENTRY_ENABLE` is 'true' and `SENTRY_DSN` is set), feature flags, queue, and JWT manager (unless in testing mode); registers before-request handler to set `g.origin_url` from `HTTP_ORIGIN` header; registers after-request handler to add version header (format `auth_api/{version}`), camelCase-convert JSON responses (except swagger.json), and set CORS headers (allow all origins, specific request headers). JWT role extraction: `get_roles()` reads `a_dict['realm_access']['roles']` and sets as `JWT_ROLE_CALLBACK`. Cache build (if not testing): clears cache, then calls `PermissionService.build_all_permission_cache()` and `ProductService.build_all_products_cache()`; swallows exceptions and logs to app.logger. Shell context processor makes `{app, jwt, db, models}` available. Incoming requests may set `registries-trace-id`, `invitation_token`, `account-id` headers.

structured.condensed:
Configuration module for a Flask authentication service that centralizes all environment variables and application settings. Loads environment values from a .env file or system variables, or provides defaults. Exports configuration objects (ProdConfig, TestConfig, DevConfig) and a factory function get_named_config() to return the appropriate config class based on environment name.

Reads from environment (or .env file): DATABASE_USERNAME, DATABASE_PASSWORD, DATABASE_NAME, DATABASE_HOST, DATABASE_PORT, DATABASE_UNIX_SOCKET; JWT_OIDC_WELL_KNOWN_CONFIG, JWT_OIDC_ALGORITHMS, JWT_OIDC_JWKS_URI, JWT_OIDC_ISSUER, JWT_OIDC_AUDIENCE, JWT_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, JWT_OIDC_CACHING_ENABLED, JWT_OIDC_JWKS_CACHE_TIMEOUT (default 300); KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALMNAME, SBC_AUTH_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID, SBC_AUTH_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET; ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFESPAN (default 300); CACHE_MEMCACHED_SERVERS, CACHE_REDIS_HOST, CACHE_REDIS_PORT; ENTITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_CLIENT_ID, ENTITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_CLIENT_SECRET; KEYCLOAK_BCROS_* settings; API endpoints (BCOL_API_URL, LEGAL_API_URL, NAMEX_API_URL, NOTIFY_API_URL, PAY_API_SANDBOX_URL, PAY_API_URL); ACCOUNT_MAILER_TOPIC (default 'account-mailer-dev'), AUTH_EVENT_TOPIC (default 'auth-event-dev'), GCP_AUTH_KEY; Minio credentials and bucket; email and token configuration; Sentry settings; WEB_APP_URL, BCEID routes; MAX_NUMBER_OF_ORGS (default 3); BCOL_ACCOUNT_LINK_CHECK (default 'True'), DIRECT_PAY_ENABLED (default 'False'), DISABLE_ACTIVITY_LOGS (default 'False'); API Gateway settings; NR_SUPPORTED_REQUEST_TYPES (default 'BC'); AUTH_WEB_SANDBOX_HOST (default 'localhost'). Catches ValueError and bare exceptions when parsing int() for JWT_OIDC_JWKS_CACHE_TIMEOUT, CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, MAX_NUMBER_OF_ORGS and silently falls back to defaults. get_named_config(config_name) raises KeyError if config_name is unknown. DevConfig sets TESTING=False, DEBUG=True, optionally disables Jaeger tracing logger.

GOTCHA: bare-except clauses swallow all exceptions silently with no logging. GOTCHA: SECRET_KEY hardcoded to 'a secret' in base class. GOTCHA: no validation that required keys (DATABASE_*, JWT_OIDC_*, KEYCLOAK_*) are actually set before use.
