structured.condensed:
Exception handling module for the auth API that wraps user and service errors with HTTP status codes and internationalization support.

**Entry points:** None—this defines exception classes only.

**BusinessException** wraps an error object and exception detail, storing `message`, `code` (from error.name), `status_code` (from error.status_code), and `detail`. On construction, it immediately calls `ExceptionTracing.trace()` with the current traceback.

**ServiceUnavailableException** wraps an error object and sets `status_code` to `Error.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.name`.

**CustomException** is a plain data object taking `message`, `status_code`, and optional `name`, used when an enum cannot be used.

No checks, no external calls on instantiation except the tracing call. Traceback is logged but exception is not retried or suppressed—it propagates to the caller.

GOTCHA: The tracing happens on every exception construction, even if the exception is caught and not re-raised.

uses.name: ExceptionTracing.trace
uses.what: Logs exception object and formatted traceback on every BusinessException construction.

uses.name: Error
uses.what: Error enum with attributes name, message, and status_code; also Error.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE constant.

structured.condensed: Configuration defining error codes and HTTP status mappings for the auth API. The Error enum provides standardized user-friendly error messages paired with HTTP response codes for invitations, user credentials, affiliations, organizations, name requests, accounts, and products. No logic or flow; pure data structure. Each enum member holds a message string and http_status constant. All 60+ error states from validation failures (INVALID_INPUT, 400), not-found (DATA_NOT_FOUND, 404), conflicts (DATA_ALREADY_EXISTS, 409), auth failures (INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS, 401), through operational constraints (MAX_NUMBER_OF_ORGS_LIMIT, DELETE_FAILED_ONLY_OWNER, OUTSTANDING_CREDIT) to service unavailability (SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, 503). Messages reference specific domains: Keycloak user creation, BC Online (BCOL) linking, Name Requests (NR) processing, affiliation invitations, GOVM accounts, product subscriptions, and payment accounts.

uses.what: HTTP status constants (HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, HTTP_409_CONFLICT, HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, HTTP_406_NOT_ACCEPTABLE) used as status_code values in enum members.

structured.condensed:
Base model superclass for database models with audit tracking.

Provides audit columns (created, modified, created_by_id, modified_by_id) that track creation and modification timestamps and users via relationships to a User model; created_by_id and modified_by_id default to the current user via _get_current_user. Entry points are public methods callable by any code. update_from_dict accepts a dict and updates model fields, skipping readonly fields (id, created, modified, created_by_id, modified_by_id), private fields starting with _, and relationship fields; returns a dict of changes as {key: {old: val, new: val}} and accepts optional _exclude list. find_by_id retrieves a model by integer id. flush adds to session, flushes, and calls create_activity. save adds, flushes, calls create_activity, and commits. delete removes, flushes, calls create_activity with is_delete=True, and commits. commit, rollback, reset, and add_to_session are passthrough session operations. create_activity creates activity records for VersionedModel instances when DISABLE_ACTIVITY_LOGS is not set, with verb 'create' or 'update' (if modified_by is not None) or 'delete', capturing preferred_username from g.jwt_oidc_token_info and remote address. _get_current_user looks up current user by JWT token and returns user.id or None; swallows all exceptions. BaseCodeModel adds code (String 15, primary key), description (String 100), and default (Boolean, False) columns; its save method commits. VersionedModel marks models as versioned with empty exclude list.

GOTCHA: _get_current_user catches all exceptions and silently returns None. GOTCHA: create_activity checks isinstance(obj, VersionedModel) but is called from methods on BaseModel itself with a BaseModel instance, meaning activity is never actually created for non-VersionedModel subclasses. GOTCHA: update_from_dict skips private fields but this chunk shows no validation that excluded fields were intended to be excluded.

structured.condensed:
User ORM model for a base-level account record in the identity and access system.

Stores users keyed by ID with username, name, email, keycloak_guid, IDP user ID, and login tracking (login_source, login_time, verified). Tracks terms-of-use acceptance, status (active/inactive via user_status_codes.id), and type (anonymous, public, gov, staff, system) derived from role. Relationships point to ContactLink, Membership (filtered to active or pending-approval), and Documents for accepted T&U version.

Entry points: find_by_username() is public classmethod with no check shown; find_by_jwt_token() decorated @user_context reads keycloak_guid and idp_userid from UserContext.token_info, this chunk shows no check; find_by_jwt_idp_userid() decorated @user_context reads idp_userid from token_info with logged error if absent, returns None if missing, this chunk shows no check; find_users() accepts first_name, last_name, email strings with no check; find_users_by_org_id_by_status_by_roles() filters by org and role with no check shown; update_terms_of_use() decorated @user_context reads is_terms_accepted boolean and terms_of_use_version foreign key, this chunk shows no check; delete() is intercepted to return self (no-op). 

create_from_jwt_token(first_name, last_name) decorated @user_context creates and saves a new User with fields from UserContext (user_name, sub, token_info email/idp_userid, login_source), sets status to UserStatusCode.get_default_type(), type via _get_type(), verified via _is_verified(login_source), this chunk shows no check.

update_from_jwt_token(user, first_name, last_name, is_login=False) decorated @user_context reads token_info, skips save if no changes detected (logic bug: condition uses OR where AND intended, checks user.username == user_from_context.user_name or user.username always true if user.username exists), updates username, firstname, lastname, email, keycloak_guid, status to ACTIVE (re-activates inactive), login_source, type, idp_userid; sets login_time if is_login=True; calls cls.commit().

_get_type() classmethod maps roles (ANONYMOUS_USER, GOV_ACCOUNT_USER, PUBLIC_USER, STAFF, SYSTEM) or login source (BCROS, BCEID, BCSC) to type name.

_is_verified() classmethod returns True only if login_source == BCSC.

GOTCHA: update_from_jwt_token() change-detection condition is malformed (uses OR instead of AND), so updates may skip save incorrectly. GOTCHA: find_users() returns all rows if all three params empty string, no pagination shown and marked TODO for scalability. GOTCHA: delete() is a no-op, violating expected ORM semantics. GOTCHA: no check shown on any classmethod that accepts user input.

structured.condensed:
Flask REST API for organization (org) management, including search, creation, retrieval, update and deletion. Requires JWT authentication with specific roles.

Entry points: (1) GET /orgs?... calls search_organizations, requires one of SYSTEM, STAFF_VIEW_ACCOUNTS, PUBLIC_USER roles; extracts name, branchName, affiliation, status, accessType, bcolAccountId, id, decisionMadeBy, orgType, page, limit from query; calls OrgService.find_by_org_name if validateName==TRUE, else OrgService.search_orgs; if caller is PUBLIC_USER without STAFF, SYSTEM or ACCOUNT_IDENTITY roles, returns empty response dict with 204 status when no results; catches BusinessException and returns code and message. (2) GET /orgs/simple?... calls search_simple_orgs, requires MANAGE_EFT or SYSTEM role (enforced by @validate_roles and @_jwt.has_one_of_roles); extracts id, page, limit, name, branchName, searchText, statuses (defaulting to ACTIVE), excludeStatuses; calls SimpleOrgService.search. (3) POST /orgs calls post_organization, requires PUBLIC_USER, STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS or SYSTEM (not ANONYMOUS_USER); validates JSON against 'org' schema; calls UserService.find_by_jwt_token, returns 401 if null; calls OrgService.create_org with request_json and user.identifier. (4) GET /orgs/<org_id> calls get_organization, requires one of SYSTEM, STAFF_VIEW_ACCOUNTS, PUBLIC_USER; calls OrgService.find_by_org_id with ALL_ALLOWED_ROLES; returns 404 if not found. (5) PUT /orgs/<org_id> calls put_organization, requires SYSTEM, PUBLIC_USER, GOV_ACCOUNT_USER or STAFF_MANAGE_ACCOUNTS; validates JSON against 'org' schema; calls OrgService.find_by_org_id with CLIENT_ADMIN_ROLES and STAFF; if org has accessType==ANONYMOUS and caller lacks STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS role, returns 401; calls org.update_org. (6) DELETE /orgs/<org_id> calls delete_organization, requires SYSTEM, STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS or PUBLIC_USER; calls OrgService.delete_org, returns 204 on success. All routes decorated with @cross_origin and @TRACER.trace(). All BusinessExceptions caught and returned as {code, message} with exception.status_code.

GOTCHA: GET /orgs?validateName=TRUE bypasses OrgSearch pagination and returns only find_by_org_name result, differing from default search behaviour. GOTCHA: PUT /orgs/<org_id> checks accessType==ANONYMOUS and STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS role but only after finding org with CLIENT_ADMIN_ROLES and STAFF filter; this allows non-matching roles to attempt update. GOTCHA: No check shown in post_organization that user actually has the role claimed by decorator, only that user was found via JWT.

Initializes and wraps the LaunchDarkly feature flag service for evaluating boolean and value flags per user in a Flask application.

Entry point: class `Flags` instantiated as module-level singleton `flags`; may be initialized via `init_app(app)` called during Flask setup. Public methods `is_on(flag, default, user)` and `value(flag, default, user)` are called to evaluate flags. The chunk shows no permission check.

On initialization: reads `AUTH_LD_SDK_KEY` from app config. If SDK key exists or app is not production, creates a LaunchDarkly config; in testing, uses local `flags.json` with `auto_update=True` and `send_events=False`; otherwise uses the SDK key directly. Stores the client in `current_app.extensions['featureflags']`.

On flag evaluation: retrieves the LaunchDarkly client; if unavailable, returns the provided default. If a User is passed, builds a Context with `user.idp_userid`, `user.firstname`, `user.lastname`; otherwise creates an anonymous context. Calls `client.variation(flag, context, default)` and returns the result as bool for `is_on()` or as-is for `value()`.

GOTCHA: no retry or fallback if LaunchDarkly client initialization fails silently; only a warning is logged.

The decorator extracts the Bearer token from the Authorization header, verifies it against Google's OAuth2 provider using the configured AUTH_AUDIENCE_SUB, and checks that the token's email_verified claim is true and its email claim is in the VERIFY_PUBSUB_EMAILS list. If verification fails or the email does not match, it aborts with 401 Unauthorized; if the token is invalid or verification raises an exception, it aborts with 400 Bad Request. On success, it calls the wrapped function with original arguments. GOTCHA: The exception handler catches all exceptions and returns a 400, collapsing token invalidity, network failures, and configuration errors into the same response.

Entry point `send_invitation()` (no check shown) constructs email data with token URL, membership role, and org details, then publishes to mailer queue; on `BusinessException`, marks invitation status 'FAILED' and re-raises. Entry point `validate_token()` (no check shown) deserializes token using `CONFIG.EMAIL_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY` and salt, checks expiry against `CONFIG.TOKEN_EXPIRY_PERIOD` (defaulting 7 days), raises `EXPIRED_INVITATION` on timeout or parse failure, then queries database for matching invitation and raises `DATA_NOT_FOUND`, `ACTIONED_INVITATION`, or `EXPIRED_INVITATION` if already accepted or expired. structured.condensed:
Service that creates, updates and retrieves Org data via the Org model.

Entry points: `create_org(org_info, user_id)` (static, no check shown); `create_membership(access_type, org, user_id)` (static, requires `@user_context` decorator; creates membership only if caller is not staff admin and access_type is not ANONYMOUS); `as_dict()` (instance method, no check shown). 

Flow in `create_org`: extracts mailing address, payment info, product subscriptions from input dict; validates org info via chained validators (account limit, access type, duplicate name, optionally BCOL credentials); if BCOL response present, maps BCOL details to org info and extracts profile flags; sets type to PREMIUM if access_type is GOVM; creates OrgModel; sets access_type; if access_type is GOVM, sets status to PENDING_INVITE_ACCEPT; adds contact if mailing address provided; creates membership; if product subscriptions provided, creates product subscriptions; creates subscriptions from BCOL profile; creates payment for org; checks if staff review needed (access_type is GOVN or access_type is EXTRA_PROVINCIAL/REGULAR_BCEID and no approved affidavit by user); if staff review needed, creates staff review task and sets org status to PENDING_STAFF_REVIEW; commits org; updates Keycloak groups; returns Org wrapper.

Calls: `Org._validate_and_raise_error()` chains validators `account_limit_validate`, `access_type_validate`, `duplicate_org_name_validate`, and conditionally `bcol_credentials_validate`; `OrgModel.create_from_dict()` creates model; `Org.add_contact_to_org()` saves mailing address; `Org.create_membership()` for membership; `ProductService.create_product_subscription()` with skip_auth=True; `ProductService.create_subscription_from_bcol_profile()` with profile flags; `Org._create_payment_for_org()` to create payment; `UserModel.find_by_jwt_token()` retrieves current user; `AffidavitModel.find_approved_by_user_id()` checks affidavit approval; `Org._create_staff_review_task()` creates task and sends reminder; `org.commit()` persists; `ProductService.update_org_product_keycloak_groups()` updates Keycloak.

Staff review task creation: sets org status to PENDING_STAFF_REVIEW; chooses task_type as GOVN_REVIEW if access_type is GOVN else NEW_ACCOUNT_STAFF_REVIEW; chooses action as AFFIDAVIT_REVIEW if user login_source is BCEID else ACCOUNT_REVIEW; calls `TaskService.create_task()` with task_info dict (name, relationshipId=org.id, relatedTo=user.id, dateSubmitted, relationshipType=ORG, type, action, status=OPEN, relationship_status=PENDING_STAFF_REVIEW) and do_commit=False; calls `Org.send_staff_review_account_reminder()`.

Payment settings in `_create_payment_settings()` (requires `@user_context`): builds pay_request dict with accountId=org.id, accountName (org name, optionally with branch name), branchName; adds paymentInfo with methodOfPayment if payment_method provided; adds contactInfo if mailing_address provided; if payment_method and BCOL account ID present, adds bcolAccountNumber and bcolUserId; if revenueAccount in payment_info, adds to paymentInfo; if payment_method is PAD, adds bankTransitNumber, bankInstitutionNumber, bankAccountNumber, padTosAcceptedBy=user_context.user_name; calls `RestService.get_service_account_token()` for token; POSTs to PAY_API_URL/accounts if is_new_org=True, else PUTs to PAY_API_URL/accounts/{org.id}, with token and raise_for_status=True; maps response status (200→CREATED, 202→PENDING, other→FAILED) to PaymentAccountStatus; if status not FAILED and payment_method present, publishes activity via `ActivityLogPublisher.publish_activity()`.

GOTCHA: commented-out TODO in create_org checks payment_account_status != FAILED but logic is not enforced. GOTCHA: no duplicate guard on membership creation in `create_membership`. GOTCHA: staff review task creation passes do_commit=False to TaskService but org.commit() called later; if commit fails, task persists.

Retrieves and searches organizations, refines access controls, validates BCOL account links, changes org status, and approves or rejects org applications with email notifications.

Entry points: `get_orgs(user_id, valid_statuses)` returns orgs for a user via `MembershipModel.find_orgs_for_user()`. `search_orgs(search, environment)` searches orgs; checks if caller has `Role.STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS` or `Role.STAFF_MANAGE_ACCOUNTS` to view `OrgStatus.PENDING_ACTIVATION` orgs, raises `BusinessException(Error.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS)` if not staff and requesting pending activation, otherwise calls `OrgModel.search_pending_activation_orgs()` or `OrgModel.search_org()`, returns dict with `orgs` (array of org as_dict plus first contact and optionally first invitation), `page`, `limit`, `total`. `search_orgs_by_affiliation(business_identifier, environment, excluded_org_types)` calls `OrgModel.search_orgs_by_business_identifier()`, returns dict with `orgs` and `total`. `refine_access_type(access_types)` decorated with `@user_context`, strips `AccessType.ANONYMOUS` from access_types unless caller has staff roles, returns tuple (access_types, is_staff_admin). `bcol_account_link_check(bcol_account_id, org_id)` when `BCOL_ACCOUNT_LINK_CHECK` config is true, calls `OrgModel.find_by_bcol_id()`, returns True if a different org already claims the bcol_account_id. `change_org_status(status_code, suspension_reason_code)` gets current user via `UserModel.find_by_jwt_token()`, updates org status_code, decision_made_by, and if suspended sets suspended_on to today, suspension_reason_code, calls `org_model.save()`, publishes activity via `ActivityLogPublisher.publish_activity()` with activity name and suspension_reason_description (or empty string if code not in SuspensionReasonCode enum), returns Org. `approve_or_reject(org_id, is_approved, origin_url, task_action)` gets org via `OrgModel.find_by_org_id()`, gets current user via `UserModel.find_by_jwt_token()`, if task_action equals `TaskAction.AFFIDAVIT_REVIEW.value` calls `AffidavitService.approve_or_reject()`, sets org status to ACTIVE or REJECTED, decision_made_by, decision_made_on to now, calls `org.save()`, gets admin emails via `UserService.get_admin_emails_for_org()`, sends email via `Org.send_approved_rejected_notification()` or `Org.send_approved_rejected_govm_govn_notification()` depending on access_type, logs error if no admin emails, returns Org. `send_staff_review_account_reminder(relationship_id, task_relationship_type)` gets current user via `UserModel.find_by_jwt_token()`, reads `STAFF_ADMIN_EMAIL` config, gets task via `TaskModel.find_by_task_relationship_id()`, builds review URL from origin_url and task.id, publishes to mailer queue `QueueMessageTypes.STAFF_REVIEW_ACCOUNT.value` with emailAddresses, contextUrl, userFirstName, userLastName, on exception logs error and raises `BusinessException(Error.FAILED_NOTIFICATION)`. `send_approved_rejected_notification(receipt_admin_emails, org_name, org_id, org_status, origin_url)` selects notification type based on org_status (ACTIVE or REJECTED), publishes to mailer queue with accountId, emailAddresses, contextUrl, orgName, on exception logs error and raises `BusinessException(Error.FAILED_NOTIFICATION)`.

GOTCHA: `change_org_status()` shows no permission check; comment says "only staff can do it now" but code lacks enforcement. GOTCHA: `approve_or_reject()` comment says "TODO Publish to activity stream" but only publishes for suspension. GOTCHA: Both send_*_notification methods swallow exception, log it, and re-raise as `BusinessException`; if mailer queue fails, org status persists as already saved.

structured.condensed: Invokes REST services with OAuth 2.0 authentication using bearer or custom auth headers. Entry points are public static methods `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `get`, and `call_posts_in_parallel`. The chunk shows no permission check at the entry points. `_invoke` is the main flow for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE: if no token supplied and `generate_token` is true, calls `_get_token()` to extract "Bearer " token from current request Authorization header; generates headers with content type, optional additional headers, and auth header formatted by `auth_header_type`; JSON-serializes data if content type is JSON; calls the HTTP method via `requests` library to the endpoint with timeout from `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` config (default 60s); if `raise_for_status` is true, raises on non-2xx response; catches ReqConnectionError or ConnectTimeout and raises ServiceUnavailableException; catches HTTPError and raises ServiceUnavailableException only if status >= 500, else re-raises; logs response headers and text in finally block. `get` is similar but mounts RETRY_ADAPTER to session if `retry_on_failure` is true, logs 404 only if `skip_404_logging` is false, logs response in finally block. `get_service_account_token` fetches OAuth token from Keycloak using service account credentials from config keys KEYCLOAK_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID and KEYCLOAK_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET, calls token endpoint at JWT_OIDC_ISSUER/protocol/openid-connect/token with grant_type=client_credentials, caches result by query string. `call_posts_in_parallel` calls multiple URLs concurrently via aiohttp with Bearer token, raises ServiceUnavailableException if any task is ClientConnectorError or status is not OK (HTTPStatus.OK), returns list of JSON responses. GOTCHA: `put` method docstring says "POST service" not PUT. GOTCHA: `patch` and `delete` methods do not accept `generate_token` parameter in their call to `_invoke` even though they pass it.

structured.condensed:
Service that creates, closes and updates Task records in the database, handling status changes and cascading updates to related Org, User, or Product Subscription entities.

Inputs: `task_info` dict (camelCase keys converted to snake_case), `task_id`, `remarks` list, `do_commit` boolean, `origin_url` string. Outputs: Task object wrapping the model, or exception. Flow: `create_task` constructs TaskModel from task_info, flushes to database, commits if requested; `close_task` sets status to CLOSED with remarks, commits if requested; `update_task` retrieves current user from JWT token, updates task status (defaults to COMPLETED), remarks, decision_made_by, decision_made_on, and relationship_status fields, flushes, then calls `_update_relationship` to cascade changes, commits, returns wrapped Task.

Decisions: In `_update_relationship`, branches on `relationship_type` (ORG, PRODUCT, or USER). For ORG: if not holding, calls `_update_org`; if holding and action is AFFIDAVIT_REVIEW, raises BusinessException(Error.INVALID_INPUT); otherwise sends hold notification via mailer. For PRODUCT: calls `_update_product_subscription`. For USER: if not holding, calls `_update_bceid_admin`; if holding, sends hold notification. After all branches, if approved and action is AFFIDAVIT_REVIEW, sets user.verified to True and saves. In `_notify_admin_about_hold`, branches on `is_new_bceid_admin_request`: builds route URL and retrieves emails from user contacts or admin list; publishes to mailer queue; catches any exception and raises BusinessException(Error.FAILED_NOTIFICATION). Entry point `create_task`, `close_task`, `update_task` are static or instance methods with no permission check shown.

GOTCHA: `update_task` retrieves user from JWT token but performs no explicit permission check that this user may update the task; check may be in caller. GOTCHA: `_notify_admin_about_hold` catches all exceptions but re-raises as BusinessException; original cause is logged but not preserved cleanly. GOTCHA: `user.verified` flag update in `_update_relationship` is non-transactional—happens after cascade updates; comment says "TODO Update user.verified flag" for org branch but code does update it for user branch. GOTCHA: `as_dict` is decorated with `@ServiceTracing.disable_tracing` but reason is not stated.

Extends Flask-SQLAlchemy's BaseQuery class to provide conditional filtering helper for database queries in a Flask application.

The `filter_conditionally` method accepts a search_criteria value, a model_attribute to filter on, and an optional is_like boolean flag. It returns the query object unchanged if search_criteria is None. For datetime or date instances, it filters by the date component using SQL's DATE function. When is_like is true, it casts the attribute to String and applies case-insensitive pattern matching with ILIKE and wildcard delimiters, using SQLAlchemy functions to prevent SQL injection. Otherwise it performs exact equality matching. The method returns self to enable query chaining.

GOTCHA: The comment notes LIKE searches must use SQLAlchemy functions for bind variables to mitigate SQL injection, but the exact equality branch (the final filter call) does not explicitly call out what injection protections apply there.

structured.condensed: Holds request-scoped user context extracted from JWT token and request headers in an auth API. Extracts and exposes username, name parts, bearer token, roles, subject ID, login source, and account ID from a JWT in Flask's g.jwt_oidc_token_info or Account-Id header. Provides role-checking methods: has_role() tests membership in _roles list; is_staff() checks for Role.STAFF.value; is_staff_admin() checks for Role.STAFF_CREATE_ACCOUNTS.value; is_system() checks for Role.SYSTEM.value; is_bceid_user() compares _login_source to LoginSource.BCEID.value. The user_context() decorator wraps functions to inject a UserContext instance. Entry point _get_context() is called by the decorator and creates a fresh instance per request. The account_id property falls back to request.headers['Account-Id'] if not in token. Token extraction via _get_token() strips 'Bearer ' prefix from Authorization header; _get_token_info() reads from g.jwt_oidc_token_info. This chunk shows no permission checks on entry points or on property access.

Utility module providing helper functions for data transformation, URL encoding, email masking, and environment detection in a Flask application.

Exports six functions and one metaclass. `camelback2snake` and `snake2camelback` convert dictionary keys between camelCase and snake_case using the humps library. `digitify` extracts and returns digits from a string via regex substitution. `escape_wam_friendly_url` base64-encodes a parameter then URL-encodes it with no safe characters. `mask_email` returns an email with username and domain each masked to first two characters plus asterisks for the remainder, or the original email if input is falsy or lacks an @ separator. `extract_numbers` returns a string of only digit characters from input, or None if input is None. `get_request_environment` returns 'sandbox' if FLASK_ENV is production and AUTH_WEB_SANDBOX_HOST appears in the current request's host URL, otherwise None. `Singleton` is a metaclass implementing singleton pattern via a class-level _instances dict checked in __call__.

GOTCHA: mask_email silently returns the original email if it cannot split on exactly one @ character, rather than raising or logging a concern.

structured.condensed:
Vue component that displays and collects payment method changes (BC Online or Pre-authorized Debit) after an outstanding balance is paid.

Displays confirmation that outstanding balance is paid, then shows a form for the chosen payment type. For BC Online (PaymentTypes.BCOL): shows description, renders LinkedBCOLBanner to collect user credentials, displays a CautionBox warning that this method will soon be retired, requires userId and password. For Pre-authorized Debit (PaymentTypes.PAD): shows description, renders PADInfoForm to collect bank details, validates form validity via isPADValid. For any other type: shows error. On complete(): validates chosen type has required fields, calls verifyPAD() to validate bank info via orgStore.validatePADInfo(), builds CreateRequestBody with paymentMethod and credentials or account numbers, calls orgStore.updateOrg(), sets current org payment type, navigates to PAYMENT_OPTION page with hasPaymentChanged flag. On HTTP 400 or 409 response: displays error.response.data.message. On other errors: displays generic message. Back/Cancel button navigates to PAYMENT_OPTION. Button text changes based on paymentType. GOTCHA: error handling does not re-raise exceptions; on non-400/409 errors, isLoading is reset but no retry occurs. GOTCHA: verifyPAD() returns true if response is empty or isValid is true, proceeding despite unclear validation state.

structured.condensed:
Manages transaction list filtering, sorting and reporting for a financial services UI, and controls who sees all transactions or only their organization's: checks a user's Role and a LaunchDarkly feature flag.

Incoming: LaunchDarklyService flag `EnableDetailsFilter`; PaymentService responses for transaction list and reports; reactive form inputs for filter field and value. Outgoing: a filtered, paginated transaction list (items and total count) or error, and transaction report data or error object.

Main flow: `loadTransactionList` (debounced 200ms) resets page to 1 on new filter, checks if any filter payload field is active (dates via `endDate`, others by truthiness), sets `isActive`, removes the `lineItemsAndDetails` filter if the flag is off and replaces it with `lineItems`, calls PaymentService.getTransactions with organization ID, filters, and viewAll flag, populates `transactions.results` and `transactions.totalResults`, or logs and continues on error. `getTransactionReport` calls PaymentService.getTransactionReports with organization ID and filter payload, returns data or error object. `setViewAll` only sets `viewAll.value = true` if currentUser.roles includes `Role.ViewAllTransactions`, else logs error and returns. `clearAllFilters` resets all filter fields and calls loadTransactionList.

Entry points: `loadTransactionList`, `getTransactionReport`, `setViewAll`, `clearAllFilters` are all public; only `setViewAll` checks permission (`Role.ViewAllTransactions`).

Callouts: PaymentService.getTransactions (no auth shown) and PaymentService.getTransactionReports (no auth shown); both receive orgId and filters; no retry on error.

GOTCHA: errors from PaymentService calls are only logged; getTransactionReport returns error in data shape but loadTransactionList silently continues; no check that setViewAll's permission check actually prevented the flag change.

uses.what: organization ID, transaction filters, and viewAll boolean; no auth credentials shown

uses.name: PaymentService.getTransactionReports
uses.what: organization ID and filter payload; no auth credentials shown

uses.name: useOrgStore
uses.what: current organization

uses.name: useUserStore
uses.what: current user and their roles

uses.name: Role.ViewAllTransactions
uses.what: authorization constant checked against currentUser.roles

structured.condensed:
Static API client that retrieves business entities, filings, contacts and review data from Auth and Legal API v2 services, creates drafts and BN requests, updates folio numbers and passcodes, downloads documents, and submits continuation review results.

Entry points: all static methods are public, callable by any component; this chunk shows no permission checks. Flow: each method constructs a URL from ConfigHelper settings and a business identifier or request object, sends an HTTP request (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) via axios, and returns the AxiosResponse or extracted data. Key decisions: getBNRequests and createBNRequest differ by appending businessNumber if present; fetchFiling and fetchContinuationReview both throw "Invalid API response" if response.data.filing or response.data is falsy; downloadDocument branches on window.navigator.msSaveOrOpenBlob (IE/deprecated) versus standard blob download; searchReviews catches errors silently, logging and returning null. Credentials: axios instance includes auth headers implicitly (not shown in this chunk). Payloads: createBusiness and addContact POST a Business and Contact object; resetBusinessPasscode PATCHes businessIdentifier, passcodeResetEmail, resetPasscode; submitContinuationReviewResult POSTs status and comment; searchReviews converts ReviewFilterParams to URLSearchParams, appending array values (status) multiple times. Document download triggers browser save/open with PDF MIME type. GOTCHA: no validation that URL argument to fetchFiling is safe; no check that response has expected shape before extracting filing or review; searchReviews swallows all errors and returns null.

structured.condensed: Searches for name requests on the BusinessLookup NameRequest API by code or words. Entry point is the static `search` method; this chunk shows no check on the caller. The method constructs a URL to the NameX API endpoint `requests/search` with the query parameter, start=0, and rows=20, then calls GET. It returns the response data cast as NameRequestLookupResultIF[] after filtering for results matching the pattern `^NR \d{7}$` on the nrNum field. If the response lacks data, throws "Invalid API response"; any HTTP or network error is caught and re-raised as "Error fetching data from API: " plus the error message. No retry logic.

structured.condensed: Supplies application URLs, API endpoints, feature flags and session storage keys to multiple frontend services. Loads on every Vue initialization, populating browser session storage with service URLs for dashboard, auth, pay, status, name request, PPR, and registry components. Holds getters for forty-five environment variables and payment-type restrictions per account. Entry point `saveConfigToSessionStorage()` is called by Vue init; no check shown. Caches disabled: code commented out to fetch config on every load. Main flow: `fetchConfig()` writes ten URLs to sessionStorage keys; `paymentsAllowedPerAccountType()` returns maps of Account types to PaymentTypes arrays, branching on LaunchDarklyService flag `LDFlags.EnableCreditCardPremium` to conditionally enable credit card for PREMIUM. Routes constructed from `VUE_APP_DASHBOARD_URL`, `VUE_APP_PATH`, and other env vars; payment payee defaults to 'BC Registries and Online Services'. Stores name request applicant details in `setNrCredentials()`. GOTCHA: cache code is dead—caching is commented out but intent is unclear.

structured.condensed:
Configuration enums that define authentication tokens, roles, account types, statuses, page routes, payment states and entity types used across the system.

SessionStorageKeys enum holds browser session storage keys: KEYCLOAK_TOKEN (auth), AUTH_API_CONFIG and AUTH_API_URL (auth service endpoints), BUSINESS_ID and CURRENT_ACCOUNT (business context), LD_FLAGS (LaunchDarkly feature flags), EXTRAPROVINCIAL_USER and AUTH_GOVN_USER (user classifications), INV_TOKEN (invitation), pagination and search filter state for three dashboards (PaginationOptions, ReviewPaginationOptions, InactivePaginationOptions; OrgSearchFilter, ReviewSearchFilter, InactiveSearchFilter; and variants for short names, linked accounts, pending/rejected/inactive accounts), URLs for AUTH_API_URL, AUTH_WEB_URL, REGISTRY_HOME_URL, STATUS_API_URL, FAS_WEB_URL, NAME_REQUEST_URL, PPR_WEB_URL, SITEMINDER_LOGOUT_URL, PAY_API_URL, STATEMENTS_DOWNLOADED flag, and SESSION_SYNCED flag.

Role enum lists named role strings: staff roles (staff, create_accounts, manage_accounts, view_accounts, suspend_accounts, bcol_staff_admin), public user variants (public_user, anonymous_user), permission types (admin_edit, bn_edit, edit, basic, tester, account_holder), government user (gov_account_user), and financial roles (fas_search, view_all_transactions, manage_eft, eft_refund, create_credits, fas_refund, manage_gl_codes).

Pages enum maps route names to paths like /admin, /admin/dashboard, /staff, /staff/dashboard, plus specific tabs (active, review, rejected, invitations, suspended, inactive), account operations (setup-account, update-account, change-account), authentication flows (signin, signout, choose-authentication-method), and payment flows (make-cc-payment, payment-option, pay-outstanding-balance).

Account enum lists premium/basic/unlinked_premium/staff account types.

AccountStatus enum lists ACTIVE, INACTIVE, REJECTED, PENDING_STAFF_REVIEW, PENDING_ACTIVATION, NSF_SUSPENDED, SUSPENDED, PENDING_INVITE_ACCEPT.

SuspensionReasonCode enum (OWNER_CHANGE, DISPUTE, COURT_ORDER, FRAUDULENT, OVERDUE_EFT) and SuspensionReason enum (NSF, OVERDUE_EFT, NSF_SUSPENDED, SUSPENDED) classify suspension reasons.

IdpHint and LoginSource enums (bcros, idir, bcsc, bceid) identify authentication providers.

InvoiceStatus enum aligns with pay-api: APPROVED, CANCELLED, CREATED, CREDITED, COMPLETED (note: equals PAID but api alters from PAID to COMPLETED in postdump), DELETE_ACCEPTED, DELETED, OVERDUE, PAID, PARTIAL_PAID, PENDING, REFUND_REQUESTED, REFUNDED, SETTLEMENT_SCHED, GL_UPDATED, GL_UPDATED_REFUND.

AffiliationTypes enum (Name Request, Amalgamation Application, Incorporation Application, Continuation Application, Corporation, Registration) and LearFilingTypes enum (Amalgamation, Incorporation, Registration) classify filings.

CorpTypes enum lists entity types including BC company variants (CC, BC, ULC), partnerships (GP, CP, SP), continuation variants (C, CBEN, CCC, CUL), COLIN-era types (CR, EPR, LL, LLC, LP, UL, XL, XP, FI, PA, PAR), societies (S, CS, XS), and temporary application types (ATMP, TMP, CTMP, NR, RTMP).

NrState enum (APPROVED, DRAFT, HOLD, REJECTED, CONDITION, CONDITIONAL, REFUND_REQUESTED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, CONSUMED, PROCESSING, INPROGRESS) and NrDisplayStates enum format name request workflow states for display.

NrConditionalStates enum (R, N, Y) indicates conditional requirement status.

NrTargetTypes enum (lear, colin, onestop) and NrEntityType enum (BC, CC, CP, CR, DBA, FI, FR, GP, LL, LP, PA, PAR, SO, UL for BC entities; RLC, XCP, XCR, XLL, XLP, XSO, XUL for XPRO; INFO for submenus) classify name request targets and entity types.

GOTCHA: eslint rule disables duplicate enum values check, allowing SessionStorageKeys.PublicUser and SessionStorageKeys.Public to exist as duplicates.

structured.condensed:
Configuration file defining enums and a message map for account deactivation, affidavits, payment actions, entity statuses, and filing products.

DEACTIVATE_ACCOUNT_MESSAGE maps three prevention reasons—OUTSTANDING_CREDIT, TRANSACTIONS_IN_PROGRESS, and DEFAULT—to message identifiers (deactivateCreditAccountMsg, deactivateActiveTransactionsMsg, deactivateGenericMsg) that callers consult to show why deactivation fails.

AffidavitStatus holds four states: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED, INACTIVE. AffidavitNumberStatus defines PENDING.

PatchActions offers UPDATE_STATUS and UPDATE_ACCESS_TYPE as request operation types.

RequestTrackerType enumerates six change-request types: InformCRA, ChangeDeliveryAddress, ChangeMailingAddress, ChangeName, ChangeStatus, ChangeParty.

Product lists ten registry products: BCA, BUSINESS, BUSINESS_SEARCH, CSO, ESRA, MHR, PPR, RPPR, RPT, VS.

EntityAlertTypes covers six alert conditions: FROZEN, BAD_STANDING, LIQUIDATION, DISSOLUTION, PROCESSING, EXPIRED.

MagicLinkInvitationStatus and AffiliationInvitationStatus track invitation lifecycle—PENDING, ACCEPTED, EXPIRED, FAILED—plus magic-link-specific EXPIRED_AFFILIATION_INVITATION and ACTIONED_AFFILIATION_INVITATION. AffiliationInvitationType distinguishes REQUEST from EMAIL.

ShortNameStatus, ShortNameLinkStatus track EFT/WIRE payment-account link states: PENDING, LINKED, UNLINKED, INACTIVE. ShortNamePaymentActions offers APPLY_CREDITS, CANCEL, REVERSE. ShortNameReversePaymentErrors codes four reversal failures: INVALID_STATE, UNPAID_STATEMENT, UNPAID_STATEMENT_INVOICE, EXCEEDS_SIXTY_DAYS.

ShortNameResponseStatus, ShortNameType, EFTRefundType enumerate response outcomes, payment methods (EFT, WIRE), and refund states (APPROVED, PENDING_APPROVAL, REJECTED) with their display names.

ShortNameHistoryType and CfsAccountStatus track transaction and account states across funds receipt, refunds, invoice reversals, and account lifecycle (PENDING, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, FREEZE, PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION).

InvoluntaryDissolutionConfigNames names seven configuration keys for scheduled dissolutions.

AccountType distinguishes business, govn, individual. OrgNameLabel maps account types to display labels (Ministry Name, Government Agency Name, Legal Business Name, Account Name).

ShortNameRefundStatus, ShortNameRefundLabel define pending-refund state and display text.

structured.condensed:
SignoutView is a Vue component that handles user logout by clearing application state and redirecting to a configured destination. When mounted, the component clears all Vuex store state via replaceState({}) and resets all application stores via resetAllStores(). It delegates the actual logout UI and process to the SbcSignout child component, passing it a redirect URL.

The redirect URL is determined by the redirectbackUrl computed property: if the redirectUrl prop is empty, it defaults to ConfigHelper.getRegistryHomeURL() with '/login' appended; otherwise it uses the provided prop value. GOTCHA: the TODO comment indicates incomplete logic—"need to fix for one URL"—suggesting redirect handling may not work correctly in some cases. The component shows no permission check.

Entry point: mounted lifecycle hook, called automatically by Vue when the component is instantiated. Callouts: ConfigHelper.getRegistryHomeURL() reads configuration; resetAllStores() clears all application stores; SbcSignout component handles logout delegation.

uses.name: ConfigHelper.getRegistryHomeURL
uses.what: Reads registry home URL from configuration to construct default redirect URL for post-logout navigation.

uses.name: resetAllStores
uses.what: Clears all application stores (Pinia or other store implementations) during logout.

uses.name: SbcSignout
uses.what: Child component that performs the actual logout operation; receives redirectbackUrl prop to determine post-logout redirect destination.

uses.name: Vue
uses.what: Component lifecycle: mounted hook is called automatically when component is instantiated.

uses.name: this.$store.replaceState
uses.what: Vuex store method that clears all state by replacing it with empty object during logout.

structured.condensed: Vue component for staff review and approval/rejection of continuation authorization applications. Displays filing and review details with conditional sections for extraprovincial registrations. Entry point is the ContinuationAuthorizationReview route handler; only staff with access to this route may call it (this chunk shows no explicit permission check). Inputs: reviewId route parameter. On mount, fetches ContinuationReview by id from BusinessService.fetchContinuationReview, then fetches the linked ContinuationFiling from BusinessService.fetchFiling; if either fetch fails, shows error dialog. Renders Extraprovincial Registration card only when filing.continuationIn.mode === 'EXPRO', Home Jurisdiction Information card, and Previous Correspondence. Submit button appears only when review.status is 'AWAITING_REVIEW' or 'RESUBMITTED'. User selects reviewResult (status) and enters emailBodyText; watchers set haveUnsavedChanges flag. beforeRouteLeave intercepts navigation and alerts if unsaved changes exist. On Submit, calls BusinessService.submitContinuationReviewResult with review.id, reviewResult, and emailBodyText, then routes to STAFF_DASHBOARD and emits success toast. On error, shows dialog; no retry. On Cancel, routes back without saving. GOTCHA: beforeRouteLeave only intercepts route changes, not page unloads, so unsaved changes can be lost on page close. GOTCHA: Review fetch failure is only logged; error dialog is not shown until both fetches complete.

uses.name: BusinessService.fetchContinuationReview
uses.what: GET request with numeric reviewId; returns ContinuationReviewIF or null on catch

uses.name: BusinessService.fetchFiling
uses.what: GET request with review.filingLink URL; returns ContinuationFilingIF or null on catch

uses.name: BusinessService.submitContinuationReviewResult
uses.what: POST with review.id, ReviewStatus reviewResult value, and string emailBodyText payload

uses.name: root.$router.push
uses.what: Navigation to Pages.STAFF_DASHBOARD route on success, error dialog close, or cancel

uses.name: EventBus.$emit
uses.what: Emits 'show-toast' event with message, type, and timeout on successful submission

uses.name: ExtraprovincialRegistrationBc
uses.what: Child component receives review and filing props; renders only when isExpro is true

uses.name: HomeJurisdictionInformation
uses.what: Child component receives review and filing props

uses.name: PreviousCorrespondence
uses.what: Child component receives review and filing props

uses.name: ReviewResult
uses.what: Child component receives review and filing props; emits review-result and email-body-text events; provides validate() method called before submit

uses.name: ModalDialog
uses.what: Child component for error display; has open() and close() methods

uses.name: Pages.STAFF_DASHBOARD
uses.what: Route constant for dashboard navigation

structured.condensed:
Flask application factory and entry point for the Events Listener service, a service worker that applies filings to the Business Database structure.

Creates and configures the Flask app: loads configuration from environment (production by default), optionally initializes Sentry error tracking if `SENTRY_ENABLE` is 'true' and `SENTRY_DSN` is set, initializes the database, feature flags, cache, and GCP queue via `db.init_app()`, `flags.init_app()`, `cache.init_app()`, and `queue.init_app()`. Registers two blueprints: `worker_endpoint` at `/` and `ops_bp` at `/ops`, with `strict_slashes=False` to match routes with or without trailing slash. Logging configuration is loaded from `logging.conf` before other setup. Entry point is `create_app()`, callable by any deployment process; this chunk shows no permission check.

uses.name: DEPLOYMENT_ENV
uses.what: Environment variable read via os.getenv() to determine run_mode; defaults to 'production' if not set.

uses.name: config.get_named_config()
uses.what: Called with run_mode to load Flask app configuration.

uses.name: SENTRY_ENABLE
uses.what: Configuration key checked (as string 'true' when lowercased) to conditionally enable Sentry.

uses.name: SENTRY_DSN
uses.what: Configuration key read to provide Sentry initialization endpoint; if missing or None, Sentry is not initialized despite SENTRY_ENABLE being true.

uses.name: sentry_sdk.init()
uses.what: Called with dsn and FlaskIntegration when SENTRY_ENABLE is 'true' and SENTRY_DSN is set.

uses.name: db.init_app()
uses.what: Called with Flask app to initialize database connection from auth_api.models.

uses.name: flags.init_app()
uses.what: Called with Flask app to initialize feature flags from auth_api.services.flags.

uses.name: cache.init_app()
uses.what: Called with Flask app to initialize cache from auth_api.utils.cache.

uses.name: queue.init_app()
uses.what: Called with Flask app to initialize GCP queue from auth_api.services.gcp_queue.

uses.name: logging.conf
uses.what: Configuration file for logging setup via setup_logging(), loaded before other initialization.

structured.condensed: Generates HTML templates by substituting template parts marked with [[partname.html]] syntax into a main template file. Reads the main template from template_path/template_file_name.html, then replaces all marked placeholders with content from corresponding files in template_path/common/. Processes exactly 12 hardcoded template parts: business-dashboard-link, footer, header, initiative-notice, logo, style, fonts, bc_logo_img, bc_registry_logo_img, whitespace-16px, whitespace-24px. Substitution occurs for each part only if its file exists and has non-zero size. Returns the final substituted template code. GOTCHA: No recursive substitution support; template parts cannot contain nested [[...]] markup. GOTCHA: Substitution syntax requires exact markup [[partname.html]] with no extra spaces.

uses.name: Path.read_text
uses.what: Template file content from template_path/template_file_name.html and individual template parts from template_path/common/{partname}.html

uses.name: os.path.exists
uses.what: Checks if template part file exists in template_path/common/

uses.name: os.path.getsize
uses.what: Verifies template part file has non-zero size before processing

structured.condensed: Blueprint that processes incoming queue messages and dispatches them to email handlers. Entry point is POST / route requiring authorized queue user via ensure_authorized_queue_user. Receives CloudEvent from request, checks if already processed via PubSubMessageProcessing.find_by_cloud_event_id_and_type (records processing with timestamp, returns early if found), then routes message by type to handlers: REFUND_DRAWDOWN_REQUEST to handle_drawdown_request, PAD_ACCOUNT_CREATE to handle_pad_account_create (fetches service token), EFT_AVAILABLE_NOTIFICATION/NSF_LOCK_ACCOUNT/NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT/CONFIRMATION_PERIOD_OVER/TEAM_MODIFIED/TEAM_MEMBER_INVITED/ADMIN_REMOVED/and others to their respective handlers. Each handler checks message type, extracts accountId/emails/data from payload, calls a processor module (refund_requested/pad_confirmation/common_mailer/account_unlock/ejv_failures/etc), then sends result to process_email(). Gets logo_url from MinioService, admin/coordinator emails from get_member_emails, and formats values via format_currency/format_day_with_suffix. Returns HTTP 200 always; exceptions are logged but not re-raised. GOTCHA: broad except swallows all errors and only logs them. GOTCHA: duplicate guard via idempotency check saves message record before handlers run but does not guard handler side effects. GOTCHA: handle_other_messages called but not shown in this chunk.

structured.condensed: Sends transactional emails in response to queue messages about payments and account changes. Entry points: `handle_payment_reminder_or_due` (called when queue message type is PAYMENT_REMINDER_NOTIFICATION or PAYMENT_DUE_NOTIFICATION; no check shown), `handle_other_messages` (called for 23 other message types; no check shown), and `process_email` (called by the above; no check shown). Both handlers receive message type and email payload (org_id, recipients, template name from enum lookup, subject from enum lookup, due date, amounts, frequencies, links count, user name, product name, context URL, role, label, remarks, application date, business name, logo URL). They format values (due date to "Month Suffix Year"), call common_mailer.process with arguments, then call process_email. process_email obtains a service account token if not provided, then calls notification_service.send_email with the email dict and token; logs debug on entry, error if email dict is empty. No duplicate guard, no retry, no permission check shown.

uses.what: Enum mapping message type name to subject line value, which may be formatted with user first/last name, product name, org name, business name; no check.

uses.what: Enum mapping message type name to title value for kwargs; no check.

uses.name: RestService.get_service_account_token

structured.condensed: Queue worker that processes three types of cloud events for an authentication and authorization system. Entry point is POST / route (line 48) protected by @ensure_authorized_queue_user; accepts wrapped SimpleCloudEvent via queue.get_simple_cloud_event(). Returns 200 OK regardless of outcome to remove event from queue. Deduplicates via PubSubMessageProcessing table: checks if cloud_event_id and message_type already processed (line 61), inserts record before processing (line 65). Routes to three handlers: NAMES_EVENT calls process_name_events(); ACTIVITY_LOG calls process_activity_log(); NSF_LOCK_ACCOUNT and NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT call process_pay_lock_unlock_event(). All exceptions caught and logged (line 54) but not re-raised—event still removed from queue. process_activity_log() writes ActivityLogModel from flattened data (line 77), rolls back session on DB error (line 86) with no retry. process_pay_lock_unlock_event() fetches OrgModel by accountId; if NSF_LOCK sets org.status_code to NSF_SUSPENDED with suspended_on timestamp and suspension_reason_code, publishes to mailer unless skipNotification true; if NSF_UNLOCK sets status to ACTIVE, clears suspension_reason_code, publishes unless skipped; calls org.flush() then db.session.commit() (lines 105, 110). process_name_events() finds or creates EntityModel by nr_number, updates status and last_modified; if status DRAFT and no existing affiliation, calls PAY_API via RestService with service token to fetch payment-requests, extracts accountId from first invoice's paymentAccount, queries OrgModel by id, creates Affiliation and ActivityLog entry if org found and not GOVM access type, calls nr_entity.save() (line 132). GOTCHA: exceptions swallowed silently in worker and process_activity_log with only logging. GOTCHA: process_name_events checks affiliations with None as second parameter to find_affiliations_by_business_identifier (line 116) but intent unclear. GOTCHA: last_modified_by hardcoded to None with TODO comment (line 119).

structured.condensed:
Job to remove users from Keycloak authentication upstream realm and from a downstream Keycloak realm.

Entry point: `run(env, idp_client_id, idp_client_secret, idp_realm, kc_client_id, kc_client_secret, kc_realm, excluded_usernames)` called from `__main__` with parsed CLI arguments; this chunk shows no check. Called via command-line with `-env`, `-idp_client`, `-idp_secret`, `-idp_realm`, `-kc_client`, `-kc_secret`, `-kc_realm`, `-exclude` flags (defaults: env=dev, idp_client=auth-service-account, idp_realm=master, kc_client=sbc-auth-admin, kc_realm=fcf0kpqr, exclude=empty).

Flow: (1) Validate both idp_client_secret and kc_client_secret are provided; if not, print error and return. (2) Build base URLs from env (prod has no prefix, other envs get `-{env}` suffix): idp_base_url and kc_base_url. (3) POST to idp_token_url and kc_token_url to get admin tokens via client_credentials grant, extracting access_token. (4) GET users from `{idp_base_url}admin/realms/{idp_realm}/users`. (5) For each user: fetch role-mappings from `{idp_base_url}admin/realms/{idp_realm}/users/{user_id}/role-mappings`; exclude if username in excluded_usernames list OR if realmMappings contains role name='admin'. (6) For non-excluded users: DELETE from `{idp_base_url}admin/realms/{idp_realm}/users/{user_id}`, then GET users from `{kc_base_url}admin/realms/{kc_realm}/users?username={user_name}`, match by username=`bcros/{user_name}`, DELETE matching user from `{kc_base_url}admin/realms/{kc_realm}/users/{kc_user_id}`. Increment delete_count. (7) Print final count.

No retry, no failure recording or re-raising; requests exceptions will propagate. No duplicate guard. No validation of token responses.

uses.name: requests.post
uses.what: POST to idp_token_url and kc_token_url with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=client_credentials in form body and Content-Type=application/x-www-form-urlencoded header; no TLS validation specified.

uses.name: requests.get
uses.what: GET to idp_base_url/admin/realms/{idp_realm}/users and {idp_realm}/users/{user_id}/role-mappings and kc_base_url/admin/realms/{kc_realm}/users?username={user_name} with Bearer token in Authorization header and Content-Type=application/json.

uses.name: requests.delete
uses.what: DELETE to idp_base_url/admin/realms/{idp_realm}/users/{user_id} and kc_base_url/admin/realms/{kc_realm}/users/{kc_user_id} with Bearer token in Authorization header and Content-Type=application/json.

uses.name: argparse.ArgumentParser
uses.what: Standard library for CLI argument parsing with flags -env, -idp_client, -idp_secret, -idp_realm, -kc_client, -kc_secret, -kc_realm, -exclude.

uses.name: https://auth-keycloak{env_prefix}.pathfinder.gov.bc.ca/auth/
uses.what: Upstream IDP Keycloak service for token and user management via admin API.

(2) Build base URLs from env (prod has no prefix, other envs get `-{env}` suffix): idp_base_url and kc_base_url. Increment delete_count. (7) Print final count.

structured.condensed:
Documentation of BCOL integration in SBC-PAY: how payments and refunds flow to BCOL, how service fees are calculated and mapped to BCOL fee codes, and testing guidance.

Invoice creation flows from PAY-API through BCOL-API to BCOL WEB SERVICE using Charge Account or Debit Account SOAP methods via `POST {{pay-api-base-url}}/api/v1/payment-requests`. Refunds are manual: the refund endpoint `POST {{pay-api-base-url}}/api/v1/payment-requests/{invoiceId}/refunds` triggers a queue event to account-mailer sending to `BCOL_REFUND_REQUEST_RECIPIENTS` environment variable recipients.

Service fee amount and BCOL fee code are determined by `corp_type` and `service_fee` value: $1.50 or $1.05 maps to `bcol_code_full_service_fee`, $1 maps to `bcol_code_partial_service_fee`, $0 maps to `bcol_code_no_service_fee`. CSO uses a service account override to apply regular BCOL fee codes instead of STAFF codes, avoiding the $1 dev fee.

Testing matches payments in BCONLINE (queryable via CPRD with `SELECT TS_FEE, RATE, DEV_FEE, TOTAL_AMT FROM BCONLINE_BILLING_RECORD where key = 'REG01788290'`) against SBC-PAY invoices table or staff dashboard transaction table. Test with both billable and non-billable BCOL accounts. Outstanding: rare invoice disappearances of unknown origin (SBC-PAY or BCOL), reconciliation platform in development.

structured.condensed:
FAQ and operations guide for the BC Registry payment system, explaining architecture decisions, data model, reconciliation, and troubleshooting procedures for handling invoices, disbursements, and partner payments across EJV, PAD, and internal channels.

The system uses asyncio-based queues instead of gevent to avoid event loop conflicts. Invoices have payment_date and refund_dates fields marking when finalization feedback arrives, distinct from created_on which disbursement updates can overwrite. Large table migrations require `op.execute("set statement_timeout=20000;")` to prevent deployment timeouts over 20 seconds; if this fails, manual execution killing database connections may be needed. The codebase is migrating from Marshmallow to Cattrs serialization for performance, with Cattrs chosen for invoice batches reaching 60,000 records. BC Online service fees are configured server-side, not in payload. Disbursement debits internal GL (excluding service fees) and credits external GL or bank accounts; EJV serves Ministry partners while AP Disbursement (EFT) serves non-Ministry partners. FRCR receipt corrections require full recreation, causing multiple routing slip jobs. Stale APPROVED invoices stuck beyond 20 days can be identified by payment_method_code. PAD refunds are impossible—only credits or pre-payment cancellation work. CAS/CFS reconciliation uses CPRD queries and planned data warehousing. Missing statements are generated by date; stuck PAD invoices need CSV processing check in cas_settlements table; stuck EJV invoices need FEEDBACK file verification with CAS. Index corruption requires `REINDEX (VERBOSE) DATABASE CONCURRENTLY`. GCP PUBSUB replay requires adding specversion and datacontenttype, changing message ID, and checking the table preventing duplicates.

uses.name: asyncio queues
uses.what: Event loop; gevent causes conflicts and breaks queue functionality.

uses.name: disbursement process
uses.what: Overwrites created_on and updated_on fields; payment_date and refund_dates were added to track actual finalization.

uses.name: CFS
uses.what: Queries for amount_due to detect uncharged or unpaid invoices; part of PAD reconciliation.

uses.name: CAS
uses.what: EJV FEEDBACK files; missing or unprocessed files indicate stuck invoices.

uses.name: BC Online
uses.what: Invoice payload; service fee is excluded because it is configured server-side.

uses.name: FRCR
uses.what: Receipt corrections require full object recreation (no PATCH/PUT support), causing multiple routing slip jobs.

uses.name: CPRD
uses.what: Queries to verify BC Online service fee and reconcile BCOL payments with SBC-PAY.

uses.name: GCP PUBSUB
uses.what: Event messages with id, source, type, and data; message ID must be changed and specversion/datacontenttype added for replay to prevent duplicates.

uses.name: Marshmallow serialization
uses.what: Legacy serialization library being replaced due to performance; still in use but slower than Cattrs.

uses.name: Cattrs serialization
uses.what: Modern fast serialization used for invoice batches up to 60,000 records.

uses.name: PAD payment method
uses.what: No refund support; only credits to CFS account or cancellation before payment execution.

uses.name: PostgreSQL index
uses.what: May become corrupted requiring REINDEX CONCURRENTLY; duplicate keys must be removed during reindexing.

uses.name: ops-support repository notebooks
uses.what: pad-pending-invoice-query-cas.ipynb, partial-refund-pad.ipynb, download-pay-minio.ipynb provide operational queries and fixes.

uses.name: FTP poller pod
uses.what: EJV inbox files via oc rsync and SFTP to restart unprocessed CAS EJV feeds.

structured.condensed: Documentation of the FAS-to-CFS integration call sequences for routing slip and invoice lifecycle events. When a routing slip is created, Pay_API calls CFS_API POST /parties (with customer name), POST /accs (create BCR account), POST /sites (hardcoded values, no address provided), and POST /rcpts (receipt numbered by routing slip). When an invoice is created, Pay_API calls POST /invs (against site) then POST /rcpts/apply (apply routing slip receipt to invoice). On full cancellation: POST /rcpts/unapply then POST /invs/adjs (adjust to zero). On partial cancellation: POST /rcpts/unapply, POST /invs/adjs (partial amount), POST /rcpts/apply (reapply receipt). On refund approval: POST /rcpts/adjs with activity_name to move funds to refund revenue. On write-off (under $10): POST /rcpts/adjs with activity_name to write-off revenue. On cheque bounce: POST /rcpts/reverse (unapplies all invoices), POST /invs (new NSF fee invoice). On routing slip link: POST /rcpts/reverse (child), POST /rcpts (create parent receipt). GOTCHA: all endpoints shown lack authentication details and payload specifications; no error handling or retry logic documented; activity_name field shown as conditional but mechanism undefined; no idempotency safeguards shown.

Configuration module for Flask service. Loads environment variables from .env, defines three configuration classes (DevConfig, TestConfig, ProdConfig) selected by name, and bundles SFTP credentials and endpoints for CAS, CGI, and EFT systems plus Minio and GCP Pub/Sub settings.

Entry point: `get_named_config(config_name)` callable by any module; this chunk shows no check. Returns config class instance; raises KeyError if config_name not in ['production', 'staging', 'testing', 'development', 'default'].

Inputs: environment variables via os.getenv() with hardcoded defaults. Outputs: Flask config object exposing SFTP_CONFIGS dict with nested host, username, password, port, key paths, and passphrases for CAS/CGI/EFT; MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_ACCESS_SECRET, MINIO_BUCKET_NAME (default 'payment-sftp'), MINIO_CGI_BUCKET_NAME ('cgi-ejv'), MINIO_EFT_BUCKET_NAME ('eft-sftp'); FTP_POLLER_TOPIC (default 'ftp-poller-payment-reconciliation-dev'); AUTH_API_ENDPOINT, CFS_BASE_URL, CFS_CLIENT_ID, CFS_CLIENT_SECRET; CGI file prefixes/suffixes; SENTRY_ENABLE, SENTRY_DSN; PUB_ENABLE_MESSAGE_ORDERING (default 'True'); DEBUG and TESTING flags.

GOTCHA: SECRET_KEY in _Config hardcoded to 'a secret'; ProdConfig regenerates it via os.urandom(24) with stderr warning if env var missing. GOTCHA: CGI_INBOX_FILE_PREFIX reads from CGI_FEEDBACK_FILE_PREFIX env var (likely typo). GOTCHA: no validation of credential format or SFTP connectivity. GOTCHA: GCP_AUTH_KEY reads from 'AUTHPAY_GCP_AUTH_KEY' env var but stores under name GCP_AUTH_KEY.

Jupyter notebook documentation that generates a weekly CSV report of payment statistics. Loads libraries (datetime, Config), connects to database via Config.SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI, executes four SQL queries against payment_accounts and invoices tables, and writes results to data/weekly_pay_stats_till_YYYY-MM-DD.csv. 

Query stat_accounts_completed counts all accounts grouped by payment_method (PAD, DRAWDOWN, ONLINE_BANKING, DIRECT_PAY, CC, CASH, CHEQUE, EJV, WIRE, EFT, INTERNAL) from payment_accounts table overall. Query stat_weekly_transactions_on_each_payment_completed counts invoices with invoice_status_code IN ('PAID', 'APPROVED') and created_on in PST timezone between (current_date - 8 days) exclusive and (current_date - 1 day) inclusive, grouped by payment_method_code. Query stat_nro_weekly_completed counts NRO corp_type_code invoices with payment_method_code in the same list, status PAID or APPROVED, and created_on (UTC converted to PST) in same weekly window. Query stat_nro_total_completed counts all NRO invoices ever with those statuses and methods, no date filter. Each result appends to CSV with section header. No entry point enforcement; no permission checks shown. GOTCHA: file is opened in append mode; if script runs twice, data duplicates without guard. GOTCHA: timezone conversion only applied in NRO queries, not weekly transactions query.

Entry point `get_named_config(config_name)` returns a config object for 'production', 'staging', 'development', or 'testing'; raises KeyError for unknown names. Base class `_Config` loads from `.env` file and environment variables (e.g. `DATABASE_USERNAME`, `DATABASE_PASSWORD`, `DATABASE_NAME`, `DATABASE_HOST`, `DATABASE_PORT`, `DATABASE_UNIX_SOCKET`) and constructs PostgreSQL connection URI with fallback to TCP if no Unix socket; optional Oracle credentials; PayBC Direct Pay settings (`PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_REF_NUMBER`, `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_API_KEY`, `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_BASE_URL`, `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_CLIENT_ID`, `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_CLIENT_SECRET`); CFS API credentials and timeout; LaunchDarkly SDK key (`PAY_LD_SDK_KEY`); Keycloak service account (`SBC_AUTH_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID`, `SBC_AUTH_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET`); Auth and Notify API endpoints; GCP PubSub topics (`ACCOUNT_MAILER_TOPIC`, `AUTH_EVENT_TOPIC`) and key; Minio endpoint and credentials for EJV bucket; CGI EJV feeder config (ministry prefix, client code, supplier number, message version, disbursement description); CGI SFTP host, port, credentials, and private key location; bank account encryption key (`ACCOUNT_SECRET_KEY`); invoice cut-off times in UTC; Sentry DSN; mail notification delay in days; disbursement delay in days; PAD confirmation period; legislative timezone; and AP/BCA supplier numbers and locations. `DevConfig` inherits from `_Config` with `TESTING = False`, `DEBUG = True`. GOTCHA: `SECRET_KEY = 'a secret'` is hardcoded default, not from environment. GOTCHA: no permission check on `get_named_config()`. GOTCHA: database credentials passed in URI string without obfuscation.

structured.condensed:
Common code that publishes NSF lock and unlock account events to a GCP Pub/Sub auth queue for downstream notification. 

Two public static methods are entry points: `publish_lock_account_event` accepts a PaymentAccountModel and optional additional_emails; `publish_unlock_account_event` accepts a PaymentAccountModel. The chunk shows no permission checks. 

For lock events, it builds a payload via `_create_event_payload` containing accountId, paymentMethod (EFT), suspensionReasonCode (OVERDUE_EFT), and additionalEmails, then publishes to AUTH_EVENT_TOPIC via `gcp_queue_publisher.publish_to_queue` with source PAY_JOBS and message type NSF_LOCK_ACCOUNT. For unlock events, it publishes a simpler payload with accountId and skipNotification=True, message type NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT, same source and topic.

Both paths send to the same external queue without checking credentials. On any exception, both log to current_app.logger (error level), log a warning with account identifiers, and capture to Sentry; neither retries. GOTCHA: exceptions are silently swallowed after logging—failures do not propagate.

structured.condensed:
Utility function that uploads files to an sFTP server.

Entry point: `upload_to_ftp(local_file_path: str, trg_file_path: str)` — this chunk shows no check, any caller may invoke it. 

The function reads seven config keys from Flask's current_app: `CGI_SFTP_HOST`, `CGI_SFTP_VERIFY_HOST`, `CGI_SFTP_HOST_KEY`, `CGI_SFTP_PORT`, `CGI_SFTP_USERNAME`, `BCREG_CGI_FTP_PRIVATE_KEY_LOCATION`, `BCREG_CGI_FTP_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSPHRASE`, and optionally `CGI_SFTP_PASSWORD`. 

Flow: (1) If `CGI_SFTP_VERIFY_HOST` is 'false', disable host key verification; otherwise decode the base64 `CGI_SFTP_HOST_KEY`, create an RSAKey, and add it to connection options. (2) Build sftp_credentials with username, private_key path, and private_key_pass; if `CGI_SFTP_PASSWORD` exists, add it. (3) Connect to the sFTP host via pysftp.Connection with these credentials and options. (4) Change directory to `CGI_SFTP_DIRECTORY`, upload both local_file_path and trg_file_path using sftp_connection.put(). (5) Close the connection. Logs debug messages at start and end.

GOTCHA: No check that local_file_path or trg_file_path exist before upload; no error handling or retry logic shown; connection closes but failure propagates unhandled.

uses.name: paramiko.RSAKey
uses.what: Called with decodebytes(ftp_host_key_data) to construct a host key for verification.

uses.name: pysftp.Connection

structured.condensed: Environment configuration file for a Flask-based payment API (pay-api) development setup. Contains database connection strings for local and test PostgreSQL instances, Flask application settings, and credentials/endpoints for integrations with Keycloak authentication, Sentry error tracking, BC Online (BCOL) services, and CFS payment gateway. All production credentials are blank for local development to prevent accidental logging or external transmission. Database connections specify host localhost with ports 54332 (dev) and 54333 (test); FLASK_DEBUG and POD_TESTING are enabled. SENTRY_ENABLE is false and SENTRY_DSN is blank to suppress error reporting. JWT authentication is configured via Keycloak with issuer, audience, and JWKS caching. BCOL integrations include WSDL endpoints for user verification and profile queries, LDAP configuration, and link codes. AUTH_API_ENDPOINT and AUTH_WEB_PAY_TRANSACTION_URL reference external authentication services. CFS payment gateway credentials and PAYBC portal URL are blank. CONNECT_TIMEOUT defaults to 30 seconds; CFS_GENERATE_RANDOM_INVOICE_NUMBER is "False".

uses.name: postgresql+pg8000://postgres@localhost:54332/postgres (DATABASE_URL)
uses.what: Local PostgreSQL database connection for development; no credentials required beyond user postgres and password postgres.

uses.name: postgresql+pg8000://postgres:admin@localhost:54333/postgres (DATABASE_TEST_URL)
uses.what: Test PostgreSQL database connection; credentials are postgres:admin.

uses.name: wsgi.py (FLASK_APP)
uses.what: Flask application entry point; referenced by configuration to start the server.

uses.name: Keycloak (JWT_OIDC_ISSUER, JWT_OIDC_WELL_KNOWN_CONFIG, JWT_OIDC_AUDIENCE, JWT_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET)
uses.what: OpenID Connect configuration for JWT token validation; all values are blank in development.

uses.name: Keycloak Admin (KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_CLIENTID, KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_SECRET, KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALMNAME)
uses.what: Keycloak admin credentials and base URL for service-to-service authentication; all blank in development.

uses.name: BCOL services (BCOL_VERIFY_USER_WSDL_URL, BCOL_QUERY_PROFILE_WSDL_URL)
uses.what: WSDL endpoints for BC Online user verification and profile queries; URLs blank in development.

uses.name: BCOL LDAP (BCOL_LDAP_SERVER, BCOL_LDAP_USER_DN_PATTERN)
uses.what: LDAP server configuration for BCOL user authentication; values blank in development.

uses.name: AUTH_API_ENDPOINT
uses.what: External authentication API endpoint; blank in development.

uses.name: AUTH_WEB_PAY_TRANSACTION_URL
uses.what: External web payment transaction URL; blank in development.

uses.name: CFS payment gateway (CFS_BASE_URL, CFS_CLIENT_ID, CFS_CLIENT_SECRET)
uses.what: CFS service credentials for payment processing; all blank in development.

uses.name: Sentry.io (SENTRY_DSN)
uses.what: Error tracking endpoint; disabled (SENTRY_ENABLE=false) and DSN blank to prevent logging in development.

The upgrade() function executes in a single uncontrolled flow. It creates cfs_account table with columns: id (primary key, auto-increment), cfs_account, cfs_party, cfs_site, bank details (name, number, branch, branch_number, account_number), is_active, and account_id (foreign key to payment_account.id); adds seven non-unique indexes on account_id, bank_account_number, bank_branch, bank_branch_number, bank_name, bank_number, and cfs_account. It adds three columns to payment_account: bcol_account, bcol_user_id, payment_method (with foreign key to payment_method.code), and indexes on bcol_account and bcol_user_id. It updates all payment_account rows setting payment_method to 'CC' where null. It queries bcol_payment_account, iterates each row, and updates payment_account and invoice with bcol details and payment_method='DRAWDOWN' where bcol_user_id exists, using unparameterized SQL string interpolation. It inserts into cfs_account from credit_payment_account marking is_active=false, then queries credit_payment_account and internal_payment_account rows and updates invoice rows to set payment_account_id. It adds payment_account_id column to invoice, removes old foreign keys (credit_account_id_fkey, bcol_account_id_fkey, internal_account_id_fkey), and creates new foreign key payment_account_payment_account_id from invoice.payment_account_id to payment_account.id. Migration saves nothing before later failure; commented-out drop statements suggest incomplete cleanup. GOTCHA: Uses unparameterized string interpolation in SQL execution—SQL injection vulnerability. GOTCHA: Commented-out drop statements for internal_payment_account, credit_payment_account, bcol_payment_account indicate incomplete schema cleanup.

Database migration: Alembic revision 6f0fe9f23d8c restructures distribution code tracking by replacing batch-based tables with file-based tracking, adds disbursement status codes, and refactors service-fee distribution codes into separate records.

**Entry point:** upgrade() runs when migrating forward; downgrade() reverses it. No permission checks shown.

**Main flow:** upgrade() creates three tables: disbursement_status_codes with four codes (UPLOADED, ACKNOWLEDGED, ERRORED, COMPLETED); ejv_files tracking uploads with created_on, completed_on, is_distribution, file_ref; ejv_invoice_links joining invoices to ejv files. Drops four old tables: daily_payment_batch_links, ejv_batch_links, daily_payment_batches, ejv_batches. Renames distribution_codes.memo_name to name. Adds disbursement_distribution_code_id and service_fee_distribution_code_id foreign keys (both self-referential to distribution_codes). Queries distribution_codes for non-null service_fee_* fields; for each result, checks if a matching record exists by stob, service_line, client, project_code, responsibility_centre; if not found, inserts new distribution_codes record with created_by='alembic' and today's date, then fetches its id and updates the source record's service_fee_distribution_code_id. Sets service_fee_distribution_code_id=null where name='NSF'. Drops six service_fee_* columns. Adds invoices.disbursement_status_code foreign key to disbursement_status_codes.code.

**Decisions:** If service fee record exists (checked by stob, service_line, client, project_code, responsibility_centre, service_fee_distribution_code_id is null), uses existing id; else creates new record. Special case: NSF records nullified after migration.

**Saves:** New distribution_codes records committed after insertion via op.execute().

**GOTCHA:** SQL injection risk: string values interpolated directly into queries without escaping (service_fee_memo_name, dates, etc.). Distribution codes migration logic assumes stob+service_line+client+project_code+responsibility_centre uniquely identifies service fees but does not validate this assumption. No explicit error handling or logging shown for the migration logic steps.

GOTCHA: SQL injection vulnerability - display_name and user_name are interpolated directly into UPDATE statements without parameterization.

Entry point `create_shortname_refund` (called by user via @user_context decorator; shows no permission check) accepts shortNameId, refundAmount, and comment; validates amount > 0 else raises Error.INVALID_REFUND; creates EFTRefund record and deducts from EFTCredit via refund_eft_credits; creates EFTHistory record with current balance and is_processing=False; queries Keycloak for Role.EFT_REFUND users and sends email with ShortNameRefundEmailContent (comment, decline_reason, refund_amount, short_name_id, short_name, status=PENDING_APPROVAL, AUTH_WEB_URL link); saves history then refund; returns refund.to_dict(). Entry point `get_shortname_refunds` (no check shown) filters EFTRefundModel by statuses list. Entry point `find_refund_by_id` retrieves by id. Entry point `handle_invoice_refund` (no check shown) processes invoice refunds: if no EFTCreditInvoiceLinkModel exists, returns REFUND_REQUESTED; if PENDING status, cancels link and restores balance; if COMPLETED status, marks as PENDING_REFUND and creates new link with new link_group_id; if balance changed, creates EFTHistory record with is_processing=True; returns REFUND_REQUESTED. Helper `refund_eft_credits` deducts amount from remaining_amount in EFTCredit records in order, raises Error.INVALID_REFUND if insufficient balance. Helper `reverse_eft_credits` adds amount back to remaining_amount, raises Error.INVALID_REFUND if amount exceeds consumed credits or exceeds expected. GOTCHA: Partner disbursement logic (PartnerDisbursementsModel creation) is commented out for corp types with has_partner_disbursements flag. GOTCHA: refund_eft_credits and reverse_eft_credits show no transactional guarantee; partial updates possible if flush fails mid-loop.

structured.condensed: Updates an EFT short-name refund approval status and sends notifications. Receives refund ID and patch data (comment, status, decline_reason). Finds refund by ID; raises BusinessException if status is not PENDING_APPROVAL. Updates comment, status, decline_reason and saves. On DECLINED: reverses EFT credits via EFTRefund.reverse_eft_credits(), updates related EFTHistoryModel transaction_type to SN_REFUND_DECLINED, recalculates credit_balance, sends email to EFT_REFUND_APPROVER role recipients with subject "Declined Refund Request for Short Name {short_name}". And return_eft_credit() helper: receives EFTCreditInvoiceLinkModel; adds its amount to eft_credit.remaining_amount; raises BusinessException if remaining_amount exceeds amount; optionally updates eft_credit_link.status_code; returns eft_credit.
